item.content:encoded:
Top 5 Red Sox Playoff Performances vs. Yankees: Garrett Crochet's Brilliant 2025 Start originally appeared on NESN. Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Red Sox acquired Garrett Crochet ahead of the 2025 season to be an ace, but not everyone immediately bought in.
An injury history and limited sample size with the White Sox raised questions about whether Crochet could live up to lofty expectations in Boston, particularly as he went from a team that posted the worst record in MLB history to one with postseason expectations.
When the postseason rolled around in 2025, Crochet delivered for the Red Sox.
Here's a look back at Crochet's Game 1 start against the Yankees and why it ranks No. 5 on the all-time list of best Red Sox playoff performances against their AL East rival.
PREVIEW:Red Sox vs. Yankees Schedule, Prediction for 2026 Series
Garrett Crochet Performance vs. Yankees
In a tough environment with an energized Yankee Stadium crowd looking to get inside his head, Crochet pitched like an ace in Game 1 of the wild-card series against the Yankees in 2025.
After giving up an early solo home run to Anthony Volpe, Crochet gave the Red Sox all but four of the outs they needed, blanking the Yankees the rest of the way until he was pulled with a whopping 117 pitches.
When the Red Sox took a 2-1 lead in the seventh inning, Crochet quickly squashed any chance of a quick New York response with a 1-2-3 frame. In the eighth, Crochet struck out two of the three batters he faced before being replaced by Aroldis Chapman. At one point, he retired 17 consecutive batters.
Here's Crochet's final line:
- 7.2 IP
- 4 H
- 1 ER
- 0 BB
- 11 K
- 117 pitches
Despite a bases-loaded, no-out scare in the bottom of the ninth, Chapman closed out the Yankees in Game 1 for a 2-1 road win.
Why it Mattered
The Red Sox didn't win the series, dropping the next two games at Yankee Stadium, but that was out of Crochet's control at that point.
Brought in to be an ace for a Red Sox team that badly needed one, Crochet delivered on that promise in Game 1, setting the tone in a difficult environment with the season effectively on the line.
Beyond the dominance of 11 strikeouts and no walks, Crochet's pitch count is what might have earned him legendary status for at least one night. 117 pitches in modern baseball, whether in the regular season or postseason, is a rare feat. Not only did Crochet give the Red Sox 117 pitches, but he looked just as dominant at the end as he did at the beginning, getting his last two outs via the strikeout.
The Red Sox would have been much happier had they won one of the next two games, but Crochet's ability to set the tone on the road in that series elevated him from a talented arm into a legitimate ace.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Pedro Martinez defends Blue Jays star after contract remark controversy
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Thursday night Pedro Martinez stopped by Fenway Park, and while making the rounds the Red Sox legend held court in the back of the press box to talk about the team, his day working with elementary school students in Lawrence earlier in the afternoon, and the upcoming Red Sox-Yankees playoff rematch. But before wrapping up, he addressed one other matter close to his heart. Toronto Blue Jays slugger Vladimir Guerrero Jr., whose Hall of Fame father played with Martinez with the Montreal Expos and w
item.content:encoded:
Thursday night Pedro Martinez stopped by Fenway Park, and while making the rounds the Red Sox legend held court in the back of the press box to talk about the team, his day working with elementary school students in Lawrence earlier in the afternoon, and the upcoming Red Sox-Yankees playoff rematch.
But before wrapping up, he addressed one other matter close to his heart.
Toronto Blue Jays slugger Vladimir Guerrero Jr., whose Hall of Fame father played with Martinez with the Montreal Expos and was a fellow Dominican Republic great, recently raised eyebrows when he made comments in a Spanish-language interview suggesting that his 14-year, $500 million contract was a reward for past performance and not an investment by the Blue Jays into his future potential.
“I want people to understand one thing,” Guerrero said in Spanish, per MLB.com’s translation. “The money they gave me wasn’t for what I’m going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn’t pay me because I’m going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself: bro, they gave you all that money and you’re out here doing nothing. I try.”
Those remarks drew criticism from Blue Jays fans and from across the sport, but Martinez, who is Guerrero’s godfather, said he believes his comments were widely misinterpreted.
“What he meant was he’s got a contract probably because of the things he did and what he might do in the future,” Martinez said. “That’s a young man talking that didn’t really explain himself, he got paid based on what he did and what he might do in the future, it’s a projection.”
While Guerrero initially stood by his comments when asked on Wednesday, he addressed the matter again on Friday and apologized to fans for the impression he’d given. He said he’d also spoken to Blue Jays manager John Schneider and apologized to his teammates for the distraction the whole ordeal had caused.
“I just gave it some thought, and I felt like the comments I made the other day were not really what I wanted to say,” Guerrero said, per Keegan Matheson of MLB.com. “I felt that everyone, my fans and everyone, deserves an apology from me.”
The firestorm comes amid a disappointing season for Guerrero, who is already a six-time All-Star at age 27 and helped lead the Blue Jays to within inches of a World Series championship last fall. But after averaging nearly 32 home runs per year over his last five seasons, Guerrero has hit only nine homers this year to go along with a massive drop in production across the board.
The Blue Jays, initially a favorite to repeat as American League champions, missed the playoffs and will finish with a losing record.
Schneider stood up for Guerrero as a teammate and a leader, and Martinez, who has known Guerrero since he was a young boy, vouched for his character, insisting that he isn’t the type of person who’d rest on his laurels.
“Vlad is not that arrogant guy that’s going to be saying ‘ahh I got paid and that’s it and I’m going to sit down,’ no, Vlady’s a gamer! We all know it,” Martinez said. “So don’t let those people that want to really ruin a good player get to that point.”
Pedro on Tracy, Breslow
Among his comments Thursday, Martinez also offered high praise for Red Sox manager Chad Tracy and chief baseball officer Craig Breslow, who both recently received long-term job security that will keep them leading the organization through the end of the decade.
Tracy, the Hall of Famer said, has done a great job pressing all the right buttons and getting the most out of his young players.
“Outstanding. Outstanding. You couldn’t ask for more. If you asked for more you’re being greedy,” Martinez said. “This is a guy that quietly, under the table, has done what he needs to do, not that Alex (Cora) didn’t do it because we saw Alex do an outstanding job, but the young team that we have has somehow clicked with him.”
Martinez also was a fan of the moves Breslow made at the trade deadline to help bolster the club’s roster ahead of the playoff push.
“Breslow deserves a lot of credit for the movement he made during the deadline, for how everything is working, for the entire team and the organization,” Martinez said. “We have to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and so far the job has been done right.”
Big fan of Tolle
Since debuting for the Red Sox late in the 2025 season, Payton Tolle has endeared himself to Red Sox fans through both his dominant performances on the mound and his larger-than-life personality.
He’s won over Martinez too, who said he loves how Tolle pitches with such infectious energy and wishes he could have learned to embrace that kind of attitude during his playing days.
“I wish I could teach myself at an early age how to be like Tolle,” Martinez said. “The guy laughs, the guy pitches, the guy is a bully, the guy is big and intimidating, he’s got everything.”
Martinez said he appreciates guys like Tolle and New York Mets reliever Jefry Yan — who often performs a dramatic jumping celebration after each strikeout — for what they bring to the game. Martinez was famously as no nonsense as you could possibly be during his playing career, but despite their apparent differences Martinez also appreciates the edge Tolle pitches with as well.
“At the same time he’s out there to beat you,” Martinez said. “He’s a bully. I love him, I love him, and he’s aware of everything he’s doing, even though he’s laughing and goofing around, you see him graciously, I think he’s doing what he needs to do and even more, having fun with it, something I couldn’t do.”

item.content:encoded:
Por Alexander Gómez
La Fundación Pedro Martínez amplió su trabajo educativo en Massachusetts y República Dominicana con un programa de programación, videojuegos e inteligencia artificial que beneficiará a estudiantes de siete escuelas de Lawrence, Massachusetts.
“Nosotros creemos que el conocimiento es lo que da autoridad y cuando al ser humano podemos facilitarle herramientas para enfrentar la vida, pues es más fácil”, afirmó Carolina, quien explicó que el proyecto comenzó hace tres años y contempla alumnos de tercer y cuarto grado.
Por su parte, Pedro Martínez exhortó a la juventud latina a trabajar por sus propios objetivos y a convertirse en agentes de progreso dentro de sus comunidades, al destacar el valor de servir de ejemplo para las nuevas generaciones.
“La voz que escuchan es un vivo ejemplo de lo que nosotros podemos ser. No le estoy pidiendo que sean precisamente como yo o como Carolina, sino como ellos quieran ser”, afirmó Martínez durante al ser entrevistados por Nilson Pepén en la transmisión en español de los Medias Rojas de Boston.
Martínez, miembro del Salón de la Fama y una de las figuras dominicanas más identificadas con Boston, dijo sentirse honrado de poder representar un modelo para los jóvenes latinos y contribuir al crecimiento de la comunidad hispana.
“Que sean alguien y que ayuden a seguir trayendo nuestra comunidad latina al sendero más alto que podamos encontrar”, expresó. El exlanzador también resaltó el avance de la presencia latina en Boston desde su llegada a la ciudad en 1998 y su satisfacción por haber formado parte de ese proceso.

item.dc:creator: Michael Hurley

Yet Gasper's story will not have a postseason, after he suffered a peculiar injury in the Red Sox' third-to-last game of the season. item.content:encoded:
In a season that will be defined by impactful performances from unlikely sources, Mickey Gasper's rise was the most unbelievable of all.
Yet Gasper's story will not have a postseason, after he suffered a peculiar injury in the Red Sox' third-to-last game of the season.
In the bottom of the fifth inning on Friday afternoon, Gasper swung and missed on a curveball, immediately flexing and grabbing at his right arm on his way to the dugout. He was replaced by Connor Wong, and between games, reports indicated that Gasper's injury was serious.
After the nightcap, manager Chad Tracy confirmed that the injury does appear to be one that will make Gasper unavailable for the postseason.
"At this point, it just looks like a significant biceps injury. So, he's gonna still be seeing more doctors and stuff like that. We'll get a final conclusion, but it's a pretty significant biceps injury," Tracy said. "It's probably gonna take him out."
The 30-year-old Gasper had cooled off since his historic month of August but still figured to be a useful lefty bat for Tracy when the Red Sox take on the Yankees next week for a best-of-three series, beginning on Tuesday. Gasper was catching in Friday's matinee, which would have given Tracy more flexibility in various situations.
Gasper batted .251 with an .823 OPS in 67 games with the Red Sox this season, doing most of his damage in the month of August. That month, he batted .400 with a 1.671 OPS, belting nine extra-base hits in 30 at-bats.
Combined with Willson Contreras declaring himself unlikely to be able to play when the playoffs begin, the Red Sox' lineup has now taken serious hits on consecutive days.
The Yankees are dealing with some injuries, too, though Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham are all working toward being able to return for the postseason.

item.title: [Boston Sports Journal] Red Sox sweep doubleheader as Wilyer Abreu delivers late; Gasper likely out for Yankees
item.dc:creator: Chris Henrique
item.description: By the time the Red Sox took the field for the second game of Friday’s doubleheader, their postseason destination was already set. They still found a way to finish a long day at Fenway Park with another win. Wilyer Abreu snapped an 0-for-11 skid with a two-run double in the eighth inning, while Brayan Bello and Jedixson Paez combined for a shutout as the Red Sox completed a doubleheader sweep of the Cubs with a 2-0 victory. Boston improved to 87-74 after winning the opener, 4-3, earlier Friday.
item.content:encoded:
By the time the Red Sox took the field for the second game of Friday’s doubleheader, their postseason destination was already set.
They still found a way to finish a long day at Fenway Park with another win.
Wilyer Abreu snapped an 0-for-11 skid with a two-run double in the eighth inning, while Brayan Bello and Jedixson Paez combined for a shutout as the Red Sox completed a doubleheader sweep of the Cubs with a 2-0 victory.
Boston improved to 87-74 after winning the opener, 4-3, earlier Friday. That victory locked the Red Sox into the No. 5 seed in the American League and officially set up a rematch with the Yankees in the best-of-three Wild Card Series beginning Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
With the standings no longer a concern, the rest of the weekend is about getting ready for New York.
Abreu entered Game 2 mired in a difficult September, carrying a .622 OPS for the month. He had gone hitless in his first seven at-bats of the doubleheader, including two strikeouts, before stepping to the plate with two outs in the eighth.
This time, Abreu delivered, ripping a two-run double to break a scoreless tie and give Boston a 2-0 lead.
The hit snapped an 0-for-11 skid for Abreu, whose streaky nature has been on display over the past two months. He posted a .971 OPS in August before cooling considerably in September.
After reaching base four times and collecting three extra-base hits in Game 1, Roman Anthony went 1-for-3 with a walk in the nightcap. He finished the doubleheader 4-for-6 with two doubles, a triple and two walks. Over his last six games, Anthony is 10-for-28 (.357) with six extra-base hits.
For an offense that has struggled throughout September, getting its leadoff hitter hot heading into the postseason could provide a significant boost.
The pitching was the bigger story in Game 2, with Bello continuing his impressive turnaround by tossing four scoreless innings against the Cubs.
His season looked much different before a demotion to Triple-A Worcester. Since returning to the majors, Bello has allowed one run or fewer in 12 of his 14 appearances, posting a 2.11 ERA with 13 runs allowed over 55 1/3 innings.
Bello isn’t expected to start during the Wild Card Series, but his work since returning from Worcester has strengthened his case for a spot on the postseason roster, where he could return to his role out of the bullpen.
Paez provided length to the bullpen in Game 2, allowing Chad Tracy to rest his relievers with the travel day coming on Saturday.
The Red Sox recalled the 22-year-old between games after optioning Raymond Burgos, who earned the save with two scoreless innings in the opener.
Paez’s first appearance with Boston on Sept. 1 was one to forget. He surrendered eight runs over 3 2/3 innings against Seattle. Paez replaced Bello and tossed five scoreless innings to finish the game, limiting the Cubs to three hits without issuing a walk while striking out four.
Paez became the first Red Sox pitcher to finish a victory with at least five scoreless innings since Scott Taylor threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Yankees on Oct. 3, 1992. The right-hander is also just the fifth pitcher in franchise history to accomplish the feat within his first five career games and only the second in the last 70 years, joining Taylor.
The Red Sox finished their 2026 slate at Fenway Park with a 41-39 record after sweeping Friday’s doubleheader. Boston also secured its first series victory since Sept. 15, finishing the season 24-26-2 in series play and 11-14-1 at home. The Red Sox won 18 of their final 30 series overall, including 10 of their final 16 at home dating to June 12.
With a nor’easter expected to impact New England this weekend, Major League Baseball moved Sunday’s finale to Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The Red Sox and Cubs will fly to Florida following Friday’s doubleheader and play Sunday at 3:05 p.m.
Gasper Likely Out for Wild Card Series
Mickey Gasper will likely miss the Red Sox’ Wild Card Series against the Yankees after suffering a right biceps injury during Friday’s 4-3 win over the Cubs, according to MassLive’s Chris Smith.
The Red Sox officially termed the injury “right biceps discomfort.”
Gasper started behind the plate and appeared to injure his biceps while swinging through a pitch for a strikeout in the fifth inning. He was removed immediately, with Connor Wong replacing him at catcher to begin the sixth.
“I think he’s going over to get an MRI right now,” Tracy said after the game. “He’s in some pretty good discomfort. So I don’t know exactly what it is but he struck out on that last swing and had some discomfort in his biceps.”
Following the Game 2 win, Tracy told reporters that Gasper suffered a significant biceps injury.
Chad Tracy confirms after the game that it looks like a "significant" biceps injury for Mickey Gasper.
"It's probably going to take him out."
Brutal. pic.twitter.com/ncoEQrgFhr
The timing is particularly unfortunate for Gasper, who had carved out a meaningful role in Boston’s lineup. The 30-year-old is batting .251 with 10 doubles, nine home runs and 24 RBI while making starts at catcher, first base and designated hitter.
Between Boston and Triple-A Worcester, Gasper has hit 19 home runs this season. His likely absence also creates another decision as the Red Sox construct their Wild Card roster.
Boston is expected to carry 14 position players and 12 pitchers against New York. Gasper’s injury could open a spot for

item.title: [Boston Herald] Wilyer Abreu’s two-run double helps Red Sox complete doubleheader sweep

item.content:encoded:
Wilyer Abreu has been one of Boston’s most impactful all-around players, but lately the talented right fielder has been stuck in a serious rut.
Over the past few weeks Abreu has seen his offensive production fall off a cliff. Coming into the day he was batting .177 with a .546 OPS and four extra-base hits over his last 17 games since Sept. 3, and during Friday’s doubleheader he started 0 for 7 his first seven trips to the plate.
That kind of slump will put a strain on anyone’s confidence, but after striking out in the bottom of the sixth, Abreu said he was approached by veteran teammate Sonny Gray, who gave him a badly needed pep talk.
“It helped me a lot,” Abreu said. “He’s a vet, he’s got a lot of years here and how to handle those situations, so he give me good advice to feel good with my body, with my athleticism, and trust myself, try to get my confidence back and that was huge.”
The next time up, Abreu reminded everyone at Fenway Park who he really is.
Abreu’s go-ahead two-run double in the bottom of the eighth was the difference in Friday night’s 2-0 win over the Chicago Cubs. The right fielder stepped to the plate with two on and two outs in a scoreless game and crushed an opposite-field line drive high off the Green Monster.
That swing helped the Red Sox seal the doubleheader sweep, and the two clubs will now fly to St. Petersburg to get out ahead of the impending nor’easter to finish the regular season on Sunday at Tropicana Field.
In what was likely his final appearance of the regular season, Brayan Bello capped off his season of turbulence and redemption in style. The right-hander threw four-plus scoreless innings, held the Cubs to four hits and a walk and struck out two while throwing 39 of his 58 pitches for strikes.
Bello wraps up the year with a 4.33 ERA, a deceptively average mark for what was an extraordinarily unique journey. After earning himself a demotion following a disastrous first half that saw him lose his spot in the rotation, Bello finished the season with a 2.11 ERA over 55 1/3 innings in his last 14 appearances since being called back up just prior to the All-Star break.
Following the game Bello said he’s happy and grateful for the way his season ended, adding that the whole year was a big learning experience.
“I learned not to let bad moments dictate how the next one is going to be,” Bello said via interpreter Carlos Villoria Benítez. “Also I learned how to compete in the zone, I feel like in the second half I was able to compete in the zone and beat hitters in the zone, something that I wasn’t able to do in the first half.”
Bello gave way to rookie Jedixson Paez, who was called up between the two games and who has also endured an eventful first year in the majors. The 22-year-old had never pitched above Single-A prior to this season before he was poached by the Chicago White Sox in the Rule 5 Draft, and the right-hander made three uninspiring appearances for the White Sox before he was returned to Boston.
After spending most of the season in the Red Sox minor league system, he was called back up for a spot start on Sept. 1 and got shelled, allowing eight runs in 3 2/3 innings in a loss to the Seattle Mariners. But needing to cover some innings ahead of the club’s upcoming playoff run, Paez came through and gave the Red Sox five scoreless frames in what was by far the best outing of his MLB career so far.
“The first chance he got it didn’t probably go how he wanted and he gets another opportunity and goes out there and spins five scoreless innings and attacks the zone,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “It was awesome.”
Offensively the Red Sox were stymied by Cubs starter David Peterson, who held Boston to three hits and two walks over five shutout innings. The Red Sox had runners reach third base in both the third and fourth innings but couldn’t get the go-ahead runner home.
Boston didn’t fare much better against the Cubs bullpen, but the Red Sox finally got another chance in the bottom of the eighth when Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Jahmai Jones each walked to put two men on with two outs.
That brought Abreu to the plate to face left-hander Ryan Rolison, and the outfielder smoked an opposite-field line drive 100.5 mph off the bat high off the Green Monster. Kiner-Falefa and Jones both came around to score, and that was all she wrote.
Paez returned for the top of the ninth despite initially seeming to deal with a cramping issue while warming up, but after a brief visit by the trainer, he stayed in the game and sent the Cubs down 1-2-3 to end the game.
With this weekend’s finale relocated to St. Petersburg, Fla., Friday night marked the final regular season game at Fenway Park this season. The next time the Red Sox are back in Boston, it will either be for Game 3 of the American League Divisional Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, or for the end-of-the-season press conference should the club lose to the Yankees in the Wild Card round again.
Before they even knew when and where their last game would be, Tracy told his players to prepare to spend 11 days on the road, and Abreu said the team is determined to bring playoff baseball back to Fenway Park for the first time since 2021.
“I think the fans deserve it,” Abreu said. “It’s been five years that Boston hasn’t seen any playoff games, so I think we have to give them that opportunity to see playoff games again here at Fenway Park.”
In the meantime, the Red Sox and Cubs will play one more at Tropicana Field on Sunday starting at 3:05 p.m.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Wilyer Abreu's timely hit allows Red Sox to sweep twin bill with Cubs
item.description: Wilyer Abreu broke a scoreless deadlock with a two-out, two-run double in the eighth inning, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 2-0 win and a doubleheader sweep over the visiting Chicago Cubs on Friday evening. Abreu was in a 0-for-11 slump before smacking the big hit high off the Green Monster in left-center field. Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Jahmai Jones both walked to set the stage for Abreu’s heroics, with the first walk coming off Chicago’s initial reliever Javier Assad (6-2) in an eventual loss. T
item.content:encoded:
Wilyer Abreu broke a scoreless deadlock with a two-out, two-run double in the eighth inning, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 2-0 win and a doubleheader sweep over the visiting Chicago Cubs on Friday evening.
Abreu was in a 0-for-11 slump before smacking the big hit high off the Green Monster in left-center field. Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Jahmai Jones both walked to set the stage for Abreu’s heroics, with the first walk coming off Chicago’s initial reliever Javier Assad (6-2) in an eventual loss.
The Red Sox (87-74) were limited to just four hits, but Jedixson Paez (1-1) made them stand up while dealing the final five innings en route to his first big-league win. Paez, who was recalled from Triple-A Worcester in between games, scattered three hits, struck out five and did not issue a walk in relief of starter Brayan Bello.
The Cubs (88-73) had seven hits, including two apiece by Seiya Suzuki, Michael Busch and Nico Hoerner.
After Chicago starter David Peterson fanned six across five innings of three-hit ball, Assad had struck out the heart of the Boston lineup in order in the sixth and retired the first six men he faced.
Bello escaped a near-immediate jam in the first. After striking out leadoff hitter Pete Crow-Armstrong, Suzuki walked and Busch dunked a single into shallow left field, but back-to-back outs in the air ended the threat.
The Boston righty also induced double plays to halt potential rallies after leadoff singles by Hoerner in the second and Busch in the fourth. Kiner-Falefa made a diving stop and spun a 4-6-3 ball to erase Hoerner.
Paez replaced Bello following Hoerner’s leadoff knock in the fifth. Matt Shaw lined a two-out single that ricocheted off the umpire standing up the middle before runners were stranded on the corners.
Meanwhile, the Red Sox were hitless until Kiner-Falefa opened the third with a line-drive single to center. He reached third on Anthony’s knock to right, but Peterson retired the next two.
In the fifth, a leadoff walk to Kiner-Falefa was wasted.
The teams’ season finale was moved to Sunday at a neutral location in St. Petersburg, Fla., due to inclement weather expected to impact Boston all weekend.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Los Medias Rojas de Boston pasaron la escoba a los Cachorros de Chicago, en la doble cartelera que se llevó a cabo este viernes en Fenway Park. A primera hora los Patirrojos triunfaron con pizarra de 4×3, y luego pintaron de blanco a los Oseznos, dos carreras por cero. Desafío donde lució el criollo Jedixson Páez en su retorno al Big Show.
Lee también: Justin Verlander se despedirá este sábado
Páez (1-1), ingresó al montículo en la parte baja del quinto episodio, en relevo del dominicano Brayan Bello. Completando una actuación realmente descollante.
El de Tinaquillo, se mantuvo en la lomita hasta el final del choque, dejando 5.0 entradas en las que aceptó tres imparables y recetó a cinco toleteros de Chicago. Salida que le permitió nivelar su récord en un triunfo por una caída y reducir considerablemente su efectividad de 18.90 a 10.80 luego de cinco presentaciones en el año.
La derrota fue a la cuenta del mexicano, Javier Assad (6-2), a quien en 2.1 innings lanzados le pisaron el plato en una ocasión
El también venezolano, Wilyer Abreu, fue el principal baluarte de la ofensiva del conjunto dirigido por Chad Tracy, al conectar de 4-1, con su doble 38 de la campaña y par de impulsadas, arribando a 76.
El pasar la escoba a los Cachorros mejoró el registro del conjunto de Massachussets a 87-74. Tercer lugar en la División Este de la Liga Americana.

Brayan Bello allowed four hits over four innings and rookie Jedixson Páez (1-1) gave up three hits in five innings with four strikeouts in his first big league win. item.content:encoded:
BOSTON (AP) — Wilyer Abreu hit a two-run double in the eighth inning, and the Boston Red Sox beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 Friday night to sweep a doubleheader.
Brayan Bello allowed four hits over four innings and rookie Jedixson Páez (1-1) gave up three hits in five innings with four strikeouts in his first big league win.
Other WRAL Top Stories
Chicago dropped two games back of San Diego for the top NL wild card. The Padres hosted Arizona later Friday.
Javier Assad (6-2) was the loser. Chicago starter David Petersen allowed three hits over five innings and struck out six.
In the first game, Connor Wong hit a tiebreaking double in the seventh inning, to help the Red Sox rally from a three-run deficit in a 4-3 win that clinched the No. 5 seed in the AL playoffs.
Boston will play its Wild Card Series for the second year in a row at the New York Yankees, who won last season’s best-of-three matchup 2-1. It will be the seventh Red Sox-Yankees postseason series.
Friday’s opener was originally scheduled for Sunday afternoon but was moved up because a significant storm was forecast. The series finale, which had been slated for Saturday night, will now be played on Sunday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Florida.
Up Next
Neither team had announced Sunday pitching plans.

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON — Alex Bregman didn’t want to be thinking about his facial fractures when he finally got back into game action.
He had been an inch away from a potential career-ending injury to his eye when he took a foul ball to his left cheek while standing near the on-deck circle Sunday in Cincinnati. Five days later, Bregman was back in the lineup as the Chicago Cubs designated hitter in Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader against the Boston Red Sox.
“Didn’t think about it one time,” Bregman said of his face afterward. “All I was thinking about was what I normally go through when in the batter’s box and in the dugout. The mechanics were terrible today, so hopefully just fix those and get back to crushing it.”
Bregman finished 0-for-4 with a strikeout in the Cubs’ 4-3 loss and didn’t start Game 2 on Friday at Fenway Park. He had a special double-flapped helmet ready to put on had he reached base to further protect his face.
“My hands were going back and my body was sliding forward,” Bregman said of his at-bats. “I just need to correct that real quick and be back to killing.”
The Cubs lost 2-0 in Game 2 and fell two games behind the Padres for the top National League wild-card seed, pending the Padres-Arizona Diamondbacks result later Friday in San Diego. The Cubs, who clinched a playoff berth Thursday, are in a virtual tie with the Phillies, who entered Friday as the No. 3 wild card before their game against the Tampa Bay Rays in Philadelphia. The Cubs own the tiebreaker over the Padres and Phillies.
The wild-card series, which are Tuesday-Thursday in both leagues, are a best-of-three format, with the higher seed playing host for the entire series. The Cubs need some help to catch the Padres for the top wild card, which would give them the NL’s No. 4 seed and home-field advantage in the opening series.
Bregman had been itching to get into Thursday’s game, manager Craig Counsell said. Once they got all the information from the doctors Monday, the involved parties sat and talked, ultimately eying Friday as the day that made sense for Bregman to return if everything went well. Following clearance by doctors and having two very good days of work, everything aligned for Bregman to start in his return to Boston, where he spent the 2025 season.
“It’s incredible that we’re talking about that he’s going to be in the lineup,” Counsell said. “A testament to his toughness, number one, and his just desire to play baseball. … This is a unique situation, but he feels up to go, and then the doctors have said you can go.”
Bregman’s return isn’t without risk, which the Cubs talked discussed with the veteran, but both parties felt they’ve done the best they could to minimize them moving forward.
“There was a lot of unknowns, and it was a freak injury, it’s an injury that we don’t deal with very often, that you don’t experience very often,” Counsell said. “Alex’s best trait is the man loves baseball, and he’s super competitive, and he’s relentless in his pursuit to be a little bit better, and so that just rubs off on people, and he loves it, and he talks about it nonstop.”
The Cubs built a three-run lead early in Game 1, though a stiff wind prevented Tyrone Taylor’s RBI double in the first and Miguel Amaya’s two-run double in the second — both off the Green Monster in left field — from being home runs.
Right-hander Clay Holmes wasn’t as sharp as the Cubs needed him to be. He struggled again with walks, issuing three free passes in 4 1/3 innings. That contributed to three runs (two earned) on five hits, and he struck out three.
“It comes down to filling the zone up, and when I do that, good things happen,” Holmes said. “The pitch count stays down, and I rely on my strengths, but yeah, really, it’s just filling the zone up more, and it put us in a much better place.”
Holmes has walked 15 batters in his last 19 2/3 innings spanning four starts. His walks are predominately coming against left-handed hitters.
“That’s why every single pitch matters,” Counsell said. “You get yourself in a bad count or you throw one close pitch that doesn’t quite nip the corner or whatever so that’s why every pitch is important to be competitive with.”

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON – Injuries have become an all-too-recurring theme for the Red Sox in September, and another one cropped up on Friday when the surging Mickey Gasper injured his right biceps while striking out in the fifth inning of the 4-3 win over the Cubs in Game 1 of a split doubleheader at Fenway Park.
For weeks, there has been a debate if Gasper’s recent power tear would land him a starting spot against righties in the postseason.
There’s a chance it could become a moot point, as Gasper underwent an MRI between games of the twin bill.
When Gasper struck out on a sweeper by Clay Holmes, he immediately started flexing his right arm.
“Some biceps discomfort on that swing,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “So I think he's going over to get an MRI now and he’s got some pretty good discomfort. So I don't know exactly what it is, but he struck out on that last swing and has discomfort in his bicep.”
Ten of Gasper’s 12 career homers have come in his last 33 games, starting on Aug. 17. He has a 1.082 OPS over that span, covering 106 plate appearances.
It has been a heartwarming rise for the 30-year-old Gasper, a journeyman who spent part of eight seasons in the Minor Leagues.
Gasper, who can also catch, would be an option to replace Contreras if he isn’t ready. But now, Gasper might not be ready either.
“Any time there's an injury and you got stuff going on, it creates uncertainty,” said Tracy. “Obviously we're pushing, and our hope is we get [Contreras] in there, but that creates uncertainty for sure. But as we've done most of the year, whatever actually ends up being the case with all of that, we plan to go play [good] baseball because that's what we’ve been doing all year.”

item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the final few games of the regular season, with the postseason starting up next week.
Boston has clinched a playoff spot, and they will be a wild-card team this season. The Red Sox battled back from a very slow start to the season, putting together a massive rally in the middle of the year.
The goal is to win a World Series title, and they seem to have a decent shot at getting it done. But while the players are focused on the play on the field, the front office also has its sights set on the upcoming offseason.
Even with the impending lockout likely coming to baseball, teams all over the league could try to maneuver rosters before it happens. For the Red Sox, they do have a key free agent hitting the market in ace Sonny Gray.
The veteran right-hander has been excellent for the Red Sox this year, firing a 2.79 ERA over 29 innings. Gray has helped establish the Red Sox rotation as one of the best in baseball, and he has been a major reason why the team has made the playoffs.
The right-hander has a mutual option for next season, but there has also been some retirement talk. However, given how strong of a year he has seen, the right-hander may postpone that idea, looking to land one last big contract.
Boston would surely want him back, but that all remains to be seen. But his free agency will be something to watch for the Red Sox and other potentially interested teams out there.
Sonny Gray Gets Major Free Agency Prediction
analyst Zach Buckley of Bleacher Report looked ahead to some of the bigger stars hitting the free-agent market this winter, predicting some of the outcomes. In this, Buckley has predicted that Gray will indeed return to the Red Sox following a strong season.
"It sounds like everything is on the table for the 36-year-old. Per Mass Live's Chris Cotillo, Gray could fetch a similar deal to the three-year, $75 million deal Nathan Eovaldi inked with the Texas Rangers two years back. But Cotillo also noted that Gray relayed in a recent interview with The Boston Globe he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family indicated any desire for him to do so.
"Only Gray knows what he's thinking, and since he doesn't need to make a decision right now, it's very possible even if he isn't sure. If he wants to keep playing, though, he has clearly set himself up to strike it rich in free agency," Buckley wrote.
Should Red Sox Resign Sonny Gray?
Given how dominant Gray has been, the Red Sox should try to sign him to a new deal. Even if this would be just for another year or two, having Gray around would help Boston heading into next season.
Gray has seen a lot of success with the Red Sox, and the team is a contender, so the two sides may come together. But for now, the focus will be on trying to win the World Series, with free agency in the back of everyone's mind.

item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox
catcher Mickey Gasper exited Game 1 of Friday's doubleheader against the Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park with an apparent injury after striking out in the bottom of the fifth inning.
After striking out swinging on a pitch in the dirt, Gasper walked off the field while flexing his right arm.
Boston Red Sox Catcher Mickey Gasper Leaves Chicago Cubs Game With Injury: Latest Update
Connor Wong
replaced Gasper at catcher in the sixth inning. After Gasper's strikeout, the Red Sox tied the game on a two-run single from Adley Rutschman.
This post will be updated with the latest information on the situation.
Update: Gasper left the game with right biceps discomfort, the Red Sox revealed to reporters.
From the Boston Globe's Tim Healey on X: Mickey Gasper left the game with right biceps discomfort, the Red Sox said.
Looking at Boston Red Sox Catcher Mickey Gasper
Gasper is a 30-year-old journeyman who has been a nice surprise for Boston this year.
Amid multiple stints in the minors, Gasper has slashed .251/.357/.466 with 10 home runs and 24 RBI in 225 plate appearances across 67 games with Boston this year.
The New York Yankees selected Gasper in the 27th round (No. 817 overall) of the 2018 MLB Draft out of college.
The 27th round no longer exists in the MLB Draft.
Gasper never reached the majors with New York. The Red Sox drafted the catcher in the minor-league phase of the 2023 Rule 5 Draft.
Gapser made his MLB debut with the Red Sox, his childhood team, in 2024. He went hitless in 18 at-bats with Boston in his first MLB season.
The Minnesota Twins acquired Gasper from the Red Sox in the 2024-25 offseason. He hit just .158/.257/.232 with two home runs and 11 RBI over 45 games with Minnesota.
The Twins designated Gasper over the winter. The Washington Nationals claimed him off waivers, only to DFA him nine days later, allowing the Red Sox to require the backstop via a waiver claim.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Red Sox first-base concerns grow with Mickey Gasper injury news
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: With Willson Contreras’ availability for next week’s Wild Card Series already in doubt following a hit-by-pitch to the hand on Sept. 17, the Boston Red Sox could ill afford another hit to their first-base depth. Which is exactly what happened during Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader against the visiting Chicago Cubs. Mickey Gasper, serving as catcher and batting second, did not return for the top of the sixth inning, due to right biceps discomfort. Manager Chad Tracy clarified Gasper felt the disc
item.content:encoded:
With Willson Contreras’ availability for next week’s Wild Card Series already in doubt following a hit-by-pitch to the hand on Sept. 17, the Boston Red Sox could ill afford another hit to their first-base depth.
Which is exactly what happened during Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader against the visiting Chicago Cubs. Mickey Gasper, serving as catcher and batting second, did not return for the top of the sixth inning, due to right biceps discomfort.
Manager Chad Tracy clarified Gasper felt the discomfort on the swing in his fifth-inning strikeout against Cubs starter Clay Holmes, and said he was going to get an MRI.
“He’s in some pretty good discomfort,” Tracy said.
Gasper has been one of the improbable heroes of this Red Sox season, particularly in the second half. After being recalled from Triple-A Worcester in mid-August, he hit .272 with a 1.119 OPS in 32 games entering Friday. His 22 hits in that span included all 10 of his career home runs.
Contreras has not played since taking a pitch to the top of his hand in Texas on Sept. 17. Though another CT scan on Thursday confirmed there is no fracture, the veteran infielder was unable to swing the bat the last two days due to lingering pain.
But on Friday morning, Tracy said they had not ruled out Contreras playing in the final game of the series.
“Life certainly creates uncertainty,” Tracy said of the Contreras and Gasper injuries. “But like, obviously, we’re pushing. Our hope is we can get them there.”

item.content:encoded:
Gasper will likely miss the AL Wild Card Series against the Yankees after suffering a biceps injury during the first game of Friday's doubleheader against the Cubs, Christopher Smith of MassLive.com reports.
The results of Gasper's MRI have not been disclosed, but it sounds like the Red Sox are preparing to be without him for at least the first round of the playoffs. Gasper was injured on a swinging strikeout in the fifth inning of Friday's matinee. Manager Chad Tracy said afterward that Gasper was in "some pretty good discomfort."

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox are bringing in a fresh arm for the second game of Friday’s doubleheader.
After pitching on back-to-back days and throwing a combined 61 pitches, left-hander Raymond Burgos is being optioned to clear space for rookie right-hander Jedixson Paez.
Burgos threw the final two innings of Boston’s last two games, tossing two scoreless innings in Thursday’s 1-0 loss to the Cleveland Guardians before earning the save with two scoreless innings in Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader against the Chicago Cubs.
Having taken on that level of workload Burgos likely wouldn’t have been available to pitch again until Sunday at the earliest, and he certainly wouldn’t have been an option out of the bullpen in Friday’s Game 2.
Paez has had a rocky rookie season in the majors. The 22-year-old was plucked from the Red Sox system by the Chicago White Sox in last winter’s Rule 5 Draft and made his MLB debut this past March. Paez made three appearances with the White Sox before being returned back to Boston, where he remained in the minors for the majority of the season until he was called back up for the club’s Sept. 1 game against the Seattle Mariners.
Paez allowed eight runs on 10 hits and two walks over 3 2/3 innings in that game, and through his first four big league appearances he has posted an 18.90 ERA over 6 2/3 career innings.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox’s best hitter could miss the wild-card round against the Yankees.
Boston first baseman Willson Contreras’ status is in question after he was hit on the hand by a pitch last week, and he told reporters Thursday that he can’t swing a bat without pain.
“I’m working hard with the trainers; the hand is slowly getting better,” Contreras said Thursday night, per MLB.com. “But I haven’t been able to swing the last two days. I’ll be honest with the team. I know Tuesday is a really important game. It’s a really important series, and I’ll be completely honest with the team.”
Contreras, a four-time All-Star, was hit on the knuckle of his right ring finger and pinkie on Sept. 17 and hasn’t played since.
MLB.com reported that Contreras was able to swing before Boston’s mid-week series against the Guardians but couldn’t do so on Wednesday or Thursday.
Contreras is having one of the best seasons of his big league career, hitting .276/.387/.518 with 27 home runs and 81 RBIs.
“It’s frustrating, if I’m being honest,” Contreras said. “I was hoping to swing today, and I couldn’t swing. I came into my locker just tearing up because that’s what we play for. We play to play in October, and it’s really frustrating when we’re doing the best you can do and you’re expecting to heal faster and that doesn’t happen.”
Contreras said tests didn’t find a fracture, with the lingering pain instead coming from inflammation and a bone bruise.
He plans to continue treatment over the next few days, but Contreras said he won’t force the issue if his hand still doesn’t feel right.
“Hopefully, I can swing the bat tomorrow and Saturday and go from there,” he said. “But like I said, I’m an honest guy, and if I don’t feel confident in my hand to be able to play either Sunday or Tuesday, I’ll be completely honest with the team.
“I don’t want to hurt the team in any way. I know that the guys here have been playing every single day, and I respect that. If I don’t feel good, I don’t want to take anybody’s spot. That’s my point. And the whole team is playing good, even though we lost tonight. The energy is still up. The guys can’t wait for Tuesday, and I can’t wait either. But we’ll see what happens.”
Contreras isn’t the only injured star coming into the series. The Yankees are in danger of being without Aaron Judge for at least the wild-card rivalry match.

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON, MA—The Boston Red Sox today recalled right-handed pitcher Jedixson Paez. To make room, Boston optioned left-handed pitcher Raymond Burgos following the first game of today’s doubleheader against the Chicago Cubs.
Paez, 22, has pitched in four Major League games (one start) this season with the Chicago White Sox (three games) and Red Sox (one start), his Major League debut, allowing 14 runs with three strikeouts over 6.2 innings. The right-hander has also posted a 3.69 ERA (29 ER/70.2 IP) with 82 strikeouts in 22 games (12 starts) between Double-A Portland (17 games, seven starts) and Triple-A Worcester (five starts) this season. Signed by Boston as an international free agent in January 2021, the Venezuela native owns a 3.31 ERA (139 ER/378.1 IP) with a 1.05 WHIP and 389 strikeouts in 95 career minor league games (70 starts).
Burgos, 27, earned his second save of the season in the first game of today’s doubleheader against the Cubs, tossing 2.0 scoreless innings. The left-hander owns a 4.22 ERA (10 ER/21.1 IP) in nine appearances for Boston this season. He has also pitched in 17 games (15 starts) for Worcester, recording a 5.14 ERA (40 ER/70.0 IP) with 58 strikeouts. Originally selected by Cleveland in the 18th round of the 2016 First-Year Player Draft, the Puerto Rico native owns a 4.43 ERA (11 ER/22.1 IP) in 10 career Major League games with the San Francisco Giants (2024) and Red Sox (2026).

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Roman Anthony rakes as Red Sox take Game 1 vs. Cubs
item.dc:creator: Jake Reiser
item.description: Alec Gamboa is not a starter. At least not at the Major League level caliber. But when the Red Sox needed someone to open a doubleheader on the last Friday of the regular season, they handed it to him anyway—and the Cubs made him pay for it quickly. Tyrone Taylor doubled in the first inning to put Chicago on the board. Miguel Amaya followed with a two-run double in the second. Three runs in two innings, Clay Holmes cruising, and the Sox in a hole before most of Fenway (whoever was going to brave
item.content:encoded:
Alec Gamboa is not a starter. At least not at the Major League level caliber. But when the Red Sox needed someone to open a doubleheader on the last Friday of the regular season, they handed it to him anyway—and the Cubs made him pay for it quickly.
Tyrone Taylor doubled in the first inning to put Chicago on the board. Miguel Amaya followed with a two-run double in the second. Three runs in two innings, Clay Holmes cruising, and the Sox in a hole before most of Fenway (whoever was going to brave the risk of weather) had settled into their seats.
Then the defense took over.
Caleb Durbin threw Matt Shaw out at the plate in the second inning to keep the Cubs from stretching it further. Isiah Kiner-Falefa made a sliding grab in the third. Andruw Monasterio came up with a diving catch in the fourth. Not glamorous plays in the box score, but they kept 3-0 from turning into 5-0, and that mattered later.
Roman Anthony was (finally) doing Roman Anthony things all afternoon. He went 3-for-3 with a walk and his fingerprints are on both comeback sequences that mattered. He got things started in the third when he scored on a Dansby Swanson throwing error to make it 3-1. Stayed alive. Kept the at-bats meaningful.
It stayed there until Adley Rutschman. With two on in the fifth against Caleb Thielbar, Rutschman hit a two-run double to tie the game. That's the at-bat the rest of this recap hangs on. There's no comeback without it.
The Cubs went to Aaron Civale in the seventh. Anthony tripled to right field, then Connor Wong stepped up and hit the go-ahead double. Red Sox 4, Cubs 3.
Willson Contreras didn't play game one—his hand still won't let him swing without pain. Ceddanne Rafaela sat out too. You can file away what Boston did to Chicago's depleted lineup, but you can also file away that a team down 3-0 didn't pack it in. The seventh inning happened.
Game 2 is next. They went ahead and won the first one.
Studs
Roman Anthony — 3-for-3 with a walk. On base four times. Scored on the error in the third to keep Boston in it, tripled in the seventh to set up the go-ahead, and was just relentless all afternoon. This was his game.
Adley Rutschman — utschman's two-run double off Thielbar tied it and gave the whole thing a different shape. That's what you pay for.
Connor Wong — Go-ahead double in the seventh coming in for Mickey Gasper. Simple entry in the ledger, but a needed go-ahead run.
Dud
The first two innings — Three runs on Gamboa before anyone got comfortable. Fair amount of that is on Gamboa, fair amount is just what happens when you open with a reliever and it doesn't work. The Sox survived it. They shouldn't count on that against a full-strength playoff opponent.
The wind — How many times did the wind knock balls down today? Yes for better with potential Cubbies homers knocked down, but also it's a hamper on an already struggling offense for the Sox.
Play of the Game
Rutschman's two-run double in the fifth. Down 3-1, two runners on, Cubs holding a lead that had felt comfortable since the second inning—and Rutschman turned the whole situation. That swing is why the seventh inning got to mean something.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Red Sox take Game 1 of Cubs doubleheader, cement Wild Card seeding
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: Amid whipping winds and the gathering storm off the coast, the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs embarked upon a doubleheader Friday afternoon. It looked bleak for the home team early on, as the Cubs took a 3-0 lead during Red Sox rookie left-hander Alec Gamboa’s two-inning opener. But Roman Anthony is heating up at exactly the right time. His 3 for 3 performance, with two doubles, a triple, walk and two runs carried the Red Sox to a 4-3 win in the top half of the doubleheader. The victory cemente
item.content:encoded:
Amid whipping winds and the gathering storm off the coast, the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs embarked upon a doubleheader Friday afternoon.
It looked bleak for the home team early on, as the Cubs took a 3-0 lead during Red Sox rookie left-hander Alec Gamboa’s two-inning opener.
But Roman Anthony is heating up at exactly the right time. His 3 for 3 performance, with two doubles, a triple, walk and two runs carried the Red Sox to a 4-3 win in the top half of the doubleheader.
The victory cemented the Red Sox as the second American League Wild Card team, meaning they are set for a rematch of last year’s Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium, which begins Tuesday.
“Just had to find a way to win there, and find a way to just kind of play Red Sox baseball as we’ve done all year, with crazy scheduling and different things,” Anthony said.
Left fielder Tyrone Taylor gave the Cubs an instant lead in the first, with a two-out RBI double after Gamboa’s one-out walk to right-fielder Seiya Suzuki. First baseman Michael Busch and shortstop Dansby Swanson slid headfirst into home in rapid succession when catcher Miguel Amaya doubled with one out in the second for a 3-0 lead.
Southpaw Jake Bennett, a starter for all 19 games of this rookie season, replaced Gamboa in the third. Bennett’s first major league relief effort encompassed 3 2/3 scoreless innings in which he yielded three hits, walked one and struck out one.
“He looked very comfortable, and was able to get in the zone right away,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said.
“Definitely a little bit of an adrenaline rush, but at the end of the day it’s the same game,” Bennett said of the difference between starting and relieving. “Just in the case that I have to come out of the bullpen in the wild card, just good to have some experience doing it at this level.”
Righty Greg Weissert (1 1/3 IP) and lefty Raymond Burgos (2 IP) held the Cubs off the rest of the way.
The Red Sox pitching staff entered Friday with 41 games with one or zero runs allowed, not only the most in the majors this season, but the club’s most in a season since the Live-Ball Era began in 1920. The Red Sox entered Friday with the third-best ERA in MLB. If they can hang on through the rest of the weekend, it will be their first season in the top three since 2007.
The bats have been Boston’s bigger issue this month, and most of the season, by far. Through 22 September games including Game 1 on Friday, the Red Sox are averaging 7.5 runners left on base per game, matching their dismal May mark.
Yet, the Red Sox were 2 for 13 with runners in scoring position, and left eight men on base, but they outhit the Cubs, 9-7, drew four walks and only struck out four times for an improvement over recent games.
“Quite a few guys that swung the bats well, we got tons of big hits, especially in the second part of the game,” Tracy said. “It was a really good offensive showing, for sure.”
After his wasted leadoff double in the first, Anthony scored the only Red Sox run through four innings, on Swanson’s throwing error in the bottom of the third.
Anthony’s second double off Cubs starter Clay Holmes went to better use. He followed Isiah Kiner-Falefa’s leadoff single in the fifth, and both men scored when designated hitter Adley Rutschman greeted lefty reliever Caleb Thielbar with a two-run single.
Holmes, a longtime New York Yankee, went 4 1/3 innings on 78 pitches (50 strikes). He allowed three runs, two earned, on five hits, walked three and struck out three.
Red Sox catcher Mickey Gasper was Holmes’ final batter. After striking out against Holmes for the third time, Gasper was replaced at catcher by Connor Wong for the top of the sixth due to what the Red Sox later announced as right biceps discomfort.
“He’s in some pretty good discomfort,” Tracy said of Gasper, who underwent an MRI after the game.
Wong’s entry proved otherwise fortuitous in the bottom of the seventh. His 12th double of the year rocketed down the third-base line, and Anthony, who tripled, jogged home for the go-ahead run.
That Anthony used the whole field with a double to left, double to center, and triple to right was among the most encouraging aspects of his offensive showing. Particularly as the swirling winds sent balls flying in unusual directions throughout the game.
“When I’m using that other way, that’s the biggest thing for me, I’ve had a lot of success in the past, and when I’m going well, I’m hitting it where it’s pitched, and taking advantage of that wall over there, even on windy days like today,” Anthony said. “Just kind of continue to pass it along, and try to be just a problem (for pitchers) any way that you possibly can.”
It fell to Burgos to protect the one-run lead in the ninth. The Red Sox southpaw did so with a 1-2-3 inning that included winning a 10-pitch at-bat against National League MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong for the second out.
The Red Sox are 86-74, with two regular-season games left to play.
After that, they’re on to New York.

item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: Mickey Gasper stepped up to the plate in the fifth inning on a windy day in Boston and worked the count full. He gave an aggressive swing on the sixth pitch he saw for a strikeout with two runners on base, but that isn't the worst of it. Gasper winced after his big swing. On his walk back to the Boston Red Sox's dugout, he flexed his arm and bent his elbow. He pressed his bicep, looking for an issue. A trainer examined him in the dugout before he went down the tunnel and left the game. Connor Wo
item.content:encoded:
Mickey Gasper stepped up to the plate in the fifth inning on a windy day in Boston and worked the count full. He gave an aggressive swing on the sixth pitch he saw for a strikeout with two runners on base, but that isn't the worst of it.
Gasper winced after his big swing. On his walk back to the Boston Red Sox's dugout, he flexed his arm and bent his elbow. He pressed his bicep, looking for an issue. A trainer examined him in the dugout before he went down the tunnel and left the game. Connor Wong replaced Gasper behind the dish.
Gasper left the game with biceps discomfort, according to multiple sources including Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. That's a vague diagnosis, but any further injuries are an ugly sign for the Sox. Willson Contreras has been sidelined since he was hit in the hand by a pitch on September 17, just four games after he returned from the injured list with a hamstring injury. The first baseman isn't confident he'll be available for the Wild Card round, and Boston needs all the offensive help it can get without him.
Gasper has cooled down lately, but he's recently off an incredible stint at the plate in the second half of August. He slashed .400/.571/1.100 with three doubles, six home runs and 10 RBI over 12 games last month.
Mickey Gasper pulled from first game of Cubs-Red Sox doubleheader with apparent arm injury following big swing
Even if Gasper has slowed down offensively, he's still proven a home run threat since his red-hot month. He's hit four homers in September, one as recently as September 22, while slashing .196/.328/.451.
If Gasper can't return to play this season, Boston has a few replacement options with the "stay ready" squad in Fort Myers. Romy Gonzalez was scorching with the WooSox in September to the tune of a .371/.410/.571 slash line. Braiden Ward and Tsung-Che Cheng are also there, but Gonzalez is the best pick given his MLB experience and recent heater. He also crushes lefties and the New York Yankees are sure to throw at least two the Red Sox's way during the Wild Card round.
Top prospect Franklin Arias is also part of the Fort Myers squad and he was in Boston on the night of September 24. The shortstop posted a breakout season between Double-A and Triple-A with a .323/.400/.557 28 doubles and 25 home runs over 117 games. The Red Sox have avoided calling Arias up this year when infield injuries cropped up, and they could be reluctant to do so now, in the biggest moment they've had all season.
A healthy Gasper would be a valuable bench option in the postseason, especially now that he's found his home run swing. Instead, the Red Sox have possibly been dealt another injury to work around at the worst possible time.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have already clinched a spot in the MLB playoffs and will wrap up the 2026 regular season across Friday and Saturday against the Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park.
For Boston, they’re coming off a 1-0 loss to the Cleveland Guardians on Thursday night, a game in which they decided to give star outfielder Roman Anthony the night off. He didn’t make any pinch-hit appearances during the contest.
Red Sox Announce Anthony Decision
Now, as they gear up for an afternoon game against the Cubs, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy has elected to put Anthony back into the lineup in his normal role.
He’ll bat leadoff and get the start in left field, while Mickey Gasper bats second and gets the start behind the plate for southpaw Alec Gamboa, who will start Game 1 of the doubleheader.
Here’s the full Red Sox lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Red Sox Game 1 9/25 R. Anthony LF M. Gasper C A. Rutschman DH W. Abreu RF C. Durbin 3B N. Sogard 2B J. Duran CF A. Monasterio 1B I. Kiner-Falefa SS A. Gamboa SP.”
Red Sox Game 1 9/25
R. Anthony LF
M. Gasper C
A. Rutschman DH
W. Abreu RF
C. Durbin 3B
N. Sogard 2B
J. Duran CF
A. Monasterio 1B
I. Kiner-Falefa SS
A. Gamboa SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 25, 2026
Anthony’s 2026 Season
It’s been a frustrating year two for Anthony, who is the current centerpiece of the Red Sox franchise.
He’s battled a wrist injury for the majority of the season, and while he’s moving back into form over the month of September, he’s appeared in just 52 games in 2026. He’s hitting .235 across 204 at-bats with 48 hits, five home runs, and 15 RBIs.
Looking at the Red Sox
Boston enters Friday’s doubleheader holding an 85-74 overall record. They remain just one win or a Chicago White Sox loss away from clinching the second Wild Card spot, which would match them up against the New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series.
The worst the Red Sox could fall is the third Wild Card seed. In that case, they’d play the No. 3 overall division winner in the AL.

item.content:encoded:
When the Chicago Cubs' lineup dropped on Friday morning, fans were greeted with quite the surprise.
Alex Bregman is back in his normal spot against a left-handed hitter, batting third in the order. While both Bregman and Craig Counsell implied that he could be back before the Wild Card round, no one would have blamed either party if that didn't come to fruition.
Bregman is only five days removed from a scary hospital visit. He was hit in the face with a foul ball during the Cubs' matchup with the Cincinnati Reds. Immediately grabbing at his face in pain and bleeding, Chicago's staff rushed him off the field and sent him for further testing. Bregman would later share images that revealed a black eye and swollen face. Testing revealed that he suffered multiple facial fractures.
Nevertheless, upon his return to Wrigley Field for the team's matchup with the Marlins, Bregman shared that he planned to get back in the batter's box sooner rather than later. And Counsell has now granted him that opportunity.
The Cubs will play Bregman at DH, meaning Matt Shaw will hold down the fort at third base. We've also seen Pedro Ramirez in that spot during Bregman's absence. All things considered, it will be interesting to see how the Cubs continue to handle the position. Keeping the still-healing Bregman off the field may be in his best interest, but there is also no ignoring the stakes.
Cubs Offense Needs a Bregman Boost
The Chicago Cubs offense was reminded of how much they need Alex Bregman's bat this week.
The Cubs' series with the Marlins left a lot to be desired. They scored a mere 2 runs in each of the three games, which included their playoff clincher on Thursday afternoon. As exciting as the moment was for the organization, it was hard to feel great about where the group was trending.
Obviously, you don't want to put too much pressure on Bregman in his return. It's already miraculous enough that he's back in the lineup. However, he has undoubtedly been the Cubs' second-best hitter in the second half of the season. The player the organization thought they were signing to a five-year deal has shown up in full force, providing a thrilling one-two punch with NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong.
Bregman is slashing .289/.374/.640 in his last month. This includes hitting double-digit home runs with a whopping 28 RBIs. He's also struck out only 13 times to 12 walks. To be sure, he has cooled off a bit over his last seven games, but the overall production still speaks for itself.
The Cubs may have a Wild Card slot locked in, but they still have a ton to play for over these next two days. The San Diego Padres hold a one-game lead for home-field advantage after picking up another win over the Dodgers on Thursday night. With how scorching hot they have been, Chicago would adore a sweep of the Red Sox.
The Phillies are also only one game behind tying the Cubbies, which remains something to monitor. Nevertheless, the good news remains that Chicago has the tiebreaker over each of their Wild Card competitors. In other words, even if they even the tally with San Diego, they will get another series at Wrigley Field.
A Bregman return will now give the Cubs their full group for one last push. Not to mention, regardless of what happens, it should help him get into a rhyhtm before the Wild Card battle starts up.
Sign up for our free newsletter to stay up-to-date with all things Chicago Cubs.
Elias Schuster is a sports journalist and content creator from the northern suburbs of Chicago. A graduate from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, he has covered the Bulls since 2019-20, previously serving as the editor of BN Bulls at Bleacher Nation, where he also covered the Cubs. He has been the Publisher for Bulls On SI since December of 2025-26 and has managed both the Cubs and White Sox in 2026. When he isn't typing away, Elias loves strolling the streets of Chicago for the best cozy bar or restaurant with his wife and far-too-energetic Jack Russell Terrier.

Anthony is hitting for a .235 BA, .328 OBP and .373 SLG with a 26.7% strikeout rate and an 11.6% walk rate. His OPS is .700 and he has scored 21 runs. In 232 plate appearances, he has hit five home runs and driven in 15 runs. He had a one-hit showing in his last game (1-for-4) against the Guardians.
The Cubs are sending Clay Holmes (6-8) to the mound to make his 18th start of the season. He is 6-8 with a 3.25 ERA and 75 strikeouts in 97 2/3 innings pitched.

item.content:encoded:
The Cubs got a lift ahead of their doubleheader against the Red Sox at Fenway on Friday. Third baseman Alex Bregman was in the starting lineup and hitting third for Chicago in Game 1.
Bregman was struck on the left side of the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch on Sunday and was examined at a local hospital in Cincinnati. He has seen multiple specialists and received as good of news as could be expected under the circumstances. No surgery was required and Bregman does not have any vision or concussion issues.
Following a slow start to the season, Bregman has been one of baseball’s top hitters since the All-Star break (.978 OPS in 59 games), while playing Gold Glove-caliber defense at third.

item.content:encoded:
Let’s play two!
With a nor’easter rolling into the area, the Cubs and Red Sox are looking to get ahead of the weather by playing a doubleheader Friday. The first game, with a 1:05 p.m. start, was originally Sunday’s contest. The teams will suit up again for a 5:35 p.m. first pitch in the nightcap — moved up slightly from its original 7:10 p.m. start, then again Thursday morning from a 6:05 start.
The Red Sox’ offense is still trying to find its form heading into October. Boston has lost four of five and has not scored more than two runs in any game during that stretch.
The Red Sox managed just two singles in Thursday’s 1-0 loss to the Guardians. In Wednesday’s 1-0 win, Andruw Monasterio snapped an 0-for-21 skid with an RBI single.
“Over these next three games, if you see some [offense] bust out, that would be great,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said. “We did have some quality plate appearances from certain guys, which was good to see.”
Willson Contreras sat out his sixth consecutive game. Contreras was hit in the right hand by a pitch a week ago, and said he couldn’t swing a bat the past two days. Tracy hopes to have Contreras back for postseason play when it begins Tuesday, but the first baseman gave a disappointing update about his condition.
“It’s really frustrating when you’re doing the best you can do, you’re expecting to heal faster and it doesn’t happen,” he said.
Alec Gamboa gets the nod for the Red Sox in the opener, followed by Brayan Bello in the second game. Gamboa, who has never faced the Cubs, owns a 0.50 ERA in his past 13 outings.
The Cubs are expected to start Clay Holmes and David Peterson — both midseason acquisitions from the Mets — in the Friday games.
Here’s a preview for this afternoon’s contest.
Lineups
This file will be updated with Game 2 lineups
CUBS (88-71): Crow-Armstrong CF, Suzuki RF, Bregman DH, Taylor LF, Hoerner 2B, Shaw 3B, Busch 1B, Swanson SS, Amaya C
Game 1 Pitching: RHP Clay Holmes (6-8, 3.25 ERA)
Game 2 Pitching: LHP David Peterson (9-8, 4.96 ERA)
RED SOX (85-74): Anthony LF, Gasper C, Rutschman DH, Abreu RF, Durbin 3B, Sogard 2B, Duran CF, Monasterio 1B, Kiner-Falefa SS
Game 1 Pitching: LHP Alec Gamboa (1-0, 1.16 ERA)
Game 2 Pitching: RHP Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.49 ERA)
Game 1 time: 1:05 p.m.
Game 2 time: 5:35 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Cubs vs. Gamboa: Has not faced any Cubs batters
Red Sox vs. Holmes: Wilyer Abreu 2-5, Willson Contreras 5-11, Jarren Duran 0-6, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 3-7, Ceddanne Rafaela 0-3, Adley Rutschman 2-4, Nick Sogard 0-2, Trevor Story 1-8, Connor Wong 1-3
Stat of the day: The Red Sox own a 39-39 record at home this season.
Notes: The Cubs downed the Marlins, 2-1, Thursday afternoon to secure their second straight postseason berth. ... Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh 40-homer, 40-steal player in major league history after stealing second base in the first inning. Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite, has 45 homers and 40 steals. ... The Cubs occupy the second NL wild-card spot. Chicago is a game behind the Padres and one game up on the Phillies. The top wild-card team hosts through the opening round of the playoffs.
Cam Kerry can be reached at cam.kerry@globe.com.

item.description: The Red Sox begin the postseason on Tuesday and have scored just 5 runs over the last 5 games. In other words, now would be a great time for the team's best offensive contributor to return to a lineup that desperately needs a spark. item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox begin the postseason on Tuesday and have scored just 5 runs over the last 5 games. In other words, now would be a great time for the team's best offensive contributor to return to a lineup that desperately needs a spark. But unless a miracle happens over the weekend, things aren't looking good. Willson Contreras took batting practice on Tuesday, only for his hand injury to worsen in the subsequent days. He's still struggling to grip a bat and admitted to tearing up out of frustration. "I'm doing everything that I can to come back and play with the boys and be there with the boys," he said. "But sometimes you have to listen to your body." (Tim Healey, Boston Globe)
At least Ceddanne Rafaela has returned. He should be able to give a little lift for the lineup, though he does present a conundrum for Chad Tracy, as the Sox now have too many outfielders and DHs to fit into the lineup at once. With Roman Anthony, Rafalea, and Wilyer Abreu essentially locked into starting spots, Tracy has to decide whether to prioritize Duran's glove and legs over the platoon DH production of Mickey Gasper and Jahmai Jones. (Sean McAdam, MassLive)
And all of this is occuring against the backdrop of this weekend's storm. And if you think we're done dealing with that now that MLB has moved Sunday's game to today, we're not. There is still a possibility that one or more of this weekend's games is moved to Tropicana Field in St. Pete. (Conor Ryan, Boston.com)
With the depressing news about Contreras, the team could probably use a pep talk. If so, Pedro Martinez — as someone who still believed in this team in the darkness of May — is available. "I just feel good about approaching the Yankees this time around. And [the Red Sox] are young, yes. We don't have the highest expectations about them, but man, for some reason, I just feel so positive," said the right arm of God. "I just feel so excited that this young group of guys that we have out there are able to do something special. I don't see anything wrong with these kids, and I don't see why they shouldn't give everybody knuckles. Not just the Yankees, but everybody." (Ian Browne, MLB.com)
If the Sox are going to give everybody knuckles, then Ranger Suarez is probably going to be a part of it. The offseason signing has an outstanding postseason resume, and his final 2026 stats are more or less in line with the numbers he'd been putting up in Philadelphia, even if he sounds slightly disappointed in his performance. "Obviously I think I could have done better," he said of his season. "But I was happy I was able to finish the season strong." (Peter Abraham, Boston Globe)

item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead at the trade deadline, but he fractured his wrist in his first game with the team. Mead avoided surgery, but he is in a race against the clock if he wants to return this season. Mead has been progressing toward a return and is planning to take a major step on Friday. "Curtis Mead (left wrist fracture) plans to take another step forward Friday by taking batting practice off of a machine," reported The Boston Globe's Tim Healey. "He will head to Fort Myers w
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead at the trade deadline, but he fractured his wrist in his first game with the team.
Mead avoided surgery, but he is in a race against the clock if he wants to return this season. Mead has been progressing toward a return and is planning to take a major step on Friday.
"Curtis Mead (left wrist fracture) plans to take another step forward Friday by taking batting practice off of a machine," reported The Boston Globe's Tim Healey. "He will head to Fort Myers with Crochet and potentially hit against him on Saturday, he said. He is not ruled out for the first round of the playoffs beginning Tuesday, but that deadline might be too soon."
Mead was having a career year before his injury, and getting that version of him in the lineup could be huge for the Red Sox's offense. However, if he's not at 100%, it may not be the best idea for the Red Sox to stick him in the lineup at second base in the most important series of the year.
Mead was slashing .253/.353/.498 with 17 home runs before he went down. The Red Sox's options at second base in the postseason include Andruw Monasterio, Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Nick Sogard. However, if Willson Contreras is unable to play due to his hand injury, Sogard will likely draw the starts at first base.
If Contreras can't play, Mead's presence in the lineup may become more important. The Red Sox's offense has been scuffling lately, and Mead could provide a boost in October.
