item.content:encoded:
Many of us believe he’s the best pitcher we’ve ever seen. He’s a blue-chip, first-ballot Hall of Famer, part of the Red Sox team that broke the Curse, and seen on TBS after Sox playoff games in any given October. He’ll be 55 next month and spends every year shuttling between Boston and his native Dominican Republic, when he’s not working in Atlanta. He has no regrets about saying “The Yankees are my daddy,” all those years ago, and he thinks the Red Sox have a shot to beat the Yankees in New York next week.
He is the one and only Pedro Martinez, and he’s spending Thursday in Lawrence with his wife, Carolina, launching an after-school coding program at South Lawrence East Elementary School, then engaging in a question-and-answer session with hundreds of students at Lawrence High School.
“Lawrence has been kind of forgotten a little bit,” said Martinez. “It has gotten kind of old in front of our eyes, but there is so much need. If there’s something I can really identify myself with, it is need. I grew up in those kind of needs. I’m just expressing the cry I had when I was a kid. I get excited every time I see a kid that has an opportunity to become someone.”
Martinez’s new program is designed to bridge resource gaps and enhance classroom learning for young students across Lawrence. His foundation, dedicated to transforming the lives of youth in the United States and the Dominican Republic, was started in 1998 when he joined the Sox after five-plus stellar seasons with the Dodgers and Expos.
“I got a very pleasant surprise when I got to Fenway as soon as I saw the drums and the people with the [Dominican] flag and the atmosphere kind of changing,” Martinez recalled. “Mayor [Thomas] Menino was kind enough to take me in his SUV to give me a tour around Boston, and right away I fell in love with the people … and the Latino community all over the place, and that’s when I landed in Lawrence, Lynn, Dorchester, and all those areas that continue to be linked to me.”
It was in those early Boston days that Martinez’s Fenway mound starts “became the curfew back home in the Dominican every time I pitched.”
A connection was made; an ongoing, lasting relationship because of the Pedro Martinez Foundation.
In 2026, Martinez and teammate/countryman David Ortiz are listed as “special assistants” in the fourth line of the the Red Sox’ official front office directory, just below chief baseball officer Craig Breslow. Martinez occasionally helps young Sox pitchers at spring training, but he was out of the loop when the decision was made to fire manager Alex Cora and six coaches just 27 games into the season.
“I was actually talking to Alex a couple of days before,” Martinez remembered. “When I found out, I wasn’t angry, I just couldn’t understand how everything snowballed to that point.”
Martinez’s beloved former teammate, catcher/captain Jason Varitek, was part of the purge. The Sox claimed Varitek was “reassigned,” but he hasn’t surfaced anywhere in the organization.
Does Martinez think the burned bridge will be repaired?
“I think it’s going to be OK with Jason,” said the three-time Cy Young Award winner. “Jason is a very professional person. He understands that business part, just like Alex Cora.”
What does Martinez think about the local demonization of Rafael Devers?
“This is a very misunderstood kid,” he said. “Devers is very shy. But he is legit. He’s a guy that doesn’t know how to express himself and has a hard time trusting anybody but his father. His father knows the actual truth … Devers is very respectful, a very lovely kid, but now it’s over and the team is on its way to success. … You have to learn to love Boston if you want to survive in Boston. Boston is 24/7 talking about their sports.”
Does Martinez want Payton Tolle or Sonny Gray starting Game 1?
“You don’t go wrong with either one,” he said. “Sonny is a true professional, a true competitor. I love, love Tolle. Just his amazing attitude. I love every single pitch he throws. I love everything about him.
“The Yankees are vulnerable, especially without [Aaron] Judge. I don’t think the Red Sox are intimidated by the Yankees. I think they can beat not only the Yankees but any team in baseball.”
The highlight of Martinez’s baseball career?
“Being part of the 25 that brought the trophy to Boston.”
Ever wish he never said, “The Yankees are my daddy”?
“No. I was being honest. That’s what you guys demand from all of us. The Yankees had my number at that point, and I expressed it. I will tell you in the most honest way, I got my ass kicked.”
Which brings us back to 2003, when Grady Little was fired (almost immediately) after failing to take Martinez out of the game when Pedro was past his pitch limit after seven innings of Game 7 of the ALCS at Yankee Stadium. Martinez had fanned Alfonso Soriano on his final pitch of the seventh, was at 100 pitches, and believed he was done for the night.
“[Red Sox pitching coach] Dave Wallace told me I was done after, so I didn’t put my jacket on,” said Martinez. “I had looked up in the sky and gave thanks to God for the seven innings I pitched. Our bullpen was lights out. All of a sudden Grady was like, ‘I don’t like [Alan] Embree against Nick Johnson in the eighth.’ He said, ‘You give me Nick Johnson and I got the rest of the bullpen for you.’ That’s the true story.”
Back on the mound, leading, 5-2, in the eighth, Martinez retired Johnson on a second-pitch popup to start the inning, then looked to the dugout. Nobody moved.
“Nothing happened,” recalled Martinez. “So I just kept going. I gave up a couple of line drives, and everything just snowballed after that. I thought I made a great pitch on [Jorge] Posada, but Posada blooped it [for a two-run double].”
All in all, it was four straight hits and a tie game before Little finally pulled Martinez after 23 disastrous eighth-inning pitches. Then Aaron Boone (now the Yankees’ manager) happened in the 11th.
Two summers ago, Maryland congressman Jamie Raskin wrote President Joe Biden a letter, imploring America’s tiring leader to end his reelection campaign. As part of his logic, Raskin compared Biden’s career to Martinez’s Game 7 performance, writing that there is “no shame in taking a well-deserved bow … when your arm is tired out.”
Days later, Biden pulled out of the race.
“I don’t know what to tell you about that,” chuckled Martinez. “Grady just told me, ‘Get one more out.’ That was Nick Johnson, right?”
Right.
All these years later, the wounds have healed and Martinez is on a greater mission, taking his message to Lawrence.
“I don’t have enough words to describe how grateful I am to have my opportunity through baseball and make a difference now,” said Martinez. “My message to these kids in Lawrence is that nothing in life is too far away if you have the will, if you have the passion.”
Dan Shaughnessy is a Globe columnist. He can be reached at daniel.shaughnessy@globe.com. Follow him @dan_shaughnessy.

item.title: [cleveland19.com] Gray earns 18th victory, Monasterio drives in run, and Red Sox edge Guardians 1-0
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: By KEN POWTAK Updated 10:25 PM EDT, September 23, 2026 BOSTON (AP) — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia’s Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians’ six-game winning streak. item.content:encoded:
By KEN POWTAK
Updated 10:25 PM EDT, September 23, 2026
BOSTON (AP) — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia’s Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians’ six-game winning streak.
It was just the fifth win in 13 games for the Red Sox, who clinched a playoff spot on Sunday.
The 36-year-old Gray (18-5) is in line to become the fourth Red Sox pitcher since 2000 to lead the AL in victories, joining Rick Porcello (2016), Josh Beckett (’07) and Curt Schilling (’04).
Gray allowed four singles, struck out three, walked one and lowered his ERA to 2.72.
Aroldis Chapman struck out the side in the ninth for his 35th save of the season.
Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) gave up a run on 10 hits with seven strikeouts.
The Guardians remained one game ahead of the Chicago White Sox atop the AL Central, after Chicago lost 5-4 to Kansas City on Wednesday night. The Guardians needed a win Wednesday combined with a loss by either Texas or Houston to clinch a postseason berth.
The victory came with a price for the Red Sox when center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela left with right hamstring tightness after running out a single the same day he was activated from the injured list. He had been sidelined with a right a quad strain since Sept. 3 and made a diving headlong grab on Steven Kwan, the game’s first batter.
Jarren Duran singled leading off the sixth, advanced on a groundout and barely beat left fielder Kwan’s throw with a headfirst slide on Monasterio’s hit.
Up next
Red Sox LHP Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) is slated to start the series finale Thursday. The Guardians had not named a starter.

item.title: [MLB.com] Red Sox confident in Gray, trio of Guerrero, Whitlock and Chapman as October nears
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne

item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray (18-5, 2.72 ERA) finished his marvelous regular season with another strong performance, firing six shutout innings on 77 pitches, allowing four hits and one walk while striking out three. Next start? Game 1 or 2 of next week’s AL Wild Card Series, all but certain to be at Yankee Stadium.
“He looked fantastic,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “Had his spin. Was in the zone. Was ahead in the count. He looked really good. It was good to see.”
Even better to see was the return of All-Star closer Aroldis Chapman, who hadn’t pitched since Sept. 13 because of a lat issue. All the 38-year-old did was overpower the Guardians by striking out the side (all swinging) in order on 12 pitches. That’s all it took for career save No. 402 and 35th this season.
“I felt good and happy to be able to go out there,” said Chapman. “I felt like my pitches and my stuff were very good today. So I’m happy to be back. I feel normal. I feel like I’m at 100 percent right now.”
That is certainly good news for the Red Sox, who need their closer in top form to make a deep postseason run.
“He looked sharp,” said Tracy. “That was also really good to see.”
For the first time in weeks, Tracy was able to deploy his 7-8-9 relief crew in Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Chapman. All three relievers had injuries at various times down the stretch but are trending well now.
“That was great,” said Tracy. “To be perfectly honest with you, that was kind of planned out regardless of how the game went. So to be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
And while hits with runners in scoring position (2-for-14, 11 left on base) were again a rare commodity for Boston, Andruw Monasterio broke out of an 0-for-21 slump by belting an RBI single with two outs in the sixth that scored Jarren Duran from second.
In a game in which neither team had an extra-base hit, combining instead for 17 singles, Monasterio’s knock was the difference in the ballgame.
“I was fighting myself just yesterday and tonight about my approach,” said Monasterio. “I just had to get through it. And I did it.”
In this final homestand of the regular season, the main focus for the Red Sox is having their house in order for what’s to come next week.
There was some cause for concern in that regard, as center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, after his first at-bat back from a three-week absence with a right quadriceps strain, had to exit in the top of the third with right hamstring tightness.
The Red Sox are hopeful it was a mild setback.
“I think it was just a cramp,” said Rafaela. “Maybe not hydrated enough. And I got that cramp right there and just didn't want to risk going for the double. And then, obviously, it’s Trace just trying to protect me, with big things in front of us. And so I think it's just that.”

item.title: [MLB.com] 'That's disgusting!': Chapman unleashes cartoonish-looking splitter
item.dc:creator: Jared Greenspan
item.description: Aroldis Chapman knows a thing or two about throwing a nasty pitch, mostly via his high-octane fastball. Every now and then, though, the left-hander reminds us that he has a few other tricks up his sleeve, too. Chapman, 38, struck out the side to notch his 35th save and secure a pivotal 1-0 Red Sox victory over the Guardians on Wednesday night at Fenway Park. He also used a devilish splitter to produce one of the nastiest pitches you’ll see this year. The bottom completely dropped out of the spli
item.content:encoded:
Aroldis Chapman knows a thing or two about throwing a nasty pitch, mostly via his high-octane fastball. Every now and then, though, the left-hander reminds us that he has a few other tricks up his sleeve, too.
Chapman, 38, struck out the side to notch his 35th save and secure a pivotal 1-0 Red Sox victory over the Guardians on Wednesday night at Fenway Park. He also used a devilish splitter to produce one of the nastiest pitches you’ll see this year.
The bottom completely dropped out of the splitter that Chapman threw in an 0-2 count to Guardians outfielder Angel Martínez, inducing a swing and miss for strike three. The pitch killed plenty of spin with just 1,095 rpms, which led to some particularly cartoonish movement, including 30 inches of vertical drop and 11 inches of horizontal break.
Chapman uses his splitter sparingly, throwing it just 12% of the time as the fourth offering in his four-pitch mix. But it’s been really good when he has used it, holding the opposition to a .138 batting average with a 36.2% whiff rate, entering Wednesday’s game.
Martínez was not the only Guardians hitter fooled by the pitch on Wednesday. Chapman actually recorded all three strikeouts with the splitter, fanning outfielder Jo Adell to begin the inning and infielder Angel Genao to close the game. It was the first time in Chapman’s career that he recorded three strikeouts with his splitter in the same game.
Wednesday marked Chapman’s first appearance since Sept. 13, as he worked through a lat issue over the last 10 days. He has a 1.92 ERA with 71 strikeouts in 51 2/3 innings.

item.title: [sentinelandenterprise.com] Sonny Gray’s scoreless start powers Red Sox to close win over Guardians
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: The Boston Red Sox pulled off a 1-0 series-evening win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night, despite the ongoing dearth of situational hitting that has plagued them for the last two weeks and intermittently throughout the season. Boston batters tallied 12 hits, but went 2 for 14 with runners in scoring position, and left 11 men on base in eight innings. Fortunately for the home team, Sonny Gray was on form in his final start of the regular season. The veteran right-hander tos
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox pulled off a 1-0 series-evening win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night, despite the ongoing dearth of situational hitting that has plagued them for the last two weeks and intermittently throughout the season.
Boston batters tallied 12 hits, but went 2 for 14 with runners in scoring position, and left 11 men on base in eight innings.
Fortunately for the home team, Sonny Gray was on form in his final start of the regular season. The veteran right-hander tossed six shutout innings, with four hits, one walk and three strikeouts.
Gray’s sixth scoreless start of at least six innings this year tied his single-season high first set in 2015 and matched in 2025. He is the first Red Sox pitcher to make at least six such starts in his age-36 season or older since Luis Tiant in 1977, and only the fourth in franchise history (also Cy Young, Lefty Grove).
“Just a really good pitcher,” manager Chad Tracy said of his starter. “The level of consistency for him from start to finish has been very fun to watch, and impressive.”
Though Gray’s pitch count sat at 77 (52 for strikes) after the sixth and the game remained scoreless, Tracy went to his bullpen. With Boston’s postseason ticket punched on Sunday, the short hook could suggest Gray is getting the ball for Game 1 of the Wild Card series on Tuesday.
Cleveland southpaw Foster Griffin was not nearly as adept at keeping the Red Sox off the diamond. He struck out seven and issued no walks, but yielded 10 hits in six innings of one-run ball.
Save for Jarren Duran’s leadoff single and Andruw Monasterio’s two-out RBI single in the sixth, the Red Sox bailed Griffin out every time. They were 2 for 11 RISP through his six innings. Their nine men left on base during Griffin’s start included multiple in four of the first five frames and bases-loaded in the third.
“Yeah, I mean, take the positives,” Tracy said of the offense. “I thought we swung the bat great. We actually got some hits today. … Between (the two-out hits) and the accumulation of hits and base runners throughout the game, I thought it was a pretty good offensive night. Obviously you’d like to score more, but we did take better plate appearances.”
Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman, Boston’s elite bullpen trio all season long, ensured the slim lead held until the end with a scoreless inning apiece. Tracy revealed postgame their appearances were “planned out, regardless of how the game went.”
“That was great,” Tracy said. “To be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
Duran, who replaced Ceddanne Rafaela in center field in the top of the third, led off the bottom of the eighth with a single. His subsequent steal of second made 2026 his second career season with 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases (also 2024). Duran, Mookie Betts and Jackie Jensen are the only players in franchise history with multiple 20-20 seasons.
Rafaela’s first game back from a 10-day stint on the injured list with a right quad strain began in energetic fashion. He recorded each of the first three outs, including a diving catch to rob Guardians hitter Steven Kwan of a leadoff single.
But after pulling up lame at first base on his own leadoff single in the bottom of the second, Rafaela ultimately left the game with right hamstring tightness when the inning turned over. Tracy announced postgame that Rafaela will undergo an MRI on Thursday.
“No, I think it’s more frustrating (than disappointing),” Tracy said of the Rafaela situation. “You want to see everybody get to that finish line healthy.
“So more just when you see it, you’re concerned, you know? So (we) don’t know where we’re at with it yet. Hopefully, it’s not a huge deal, but still, yeah, makes your heart jump a little bit, and we’ll see where he’s at.”
Cleveland threatened against Whitlock in an eighth inning that saw both teams run out of ABS challenges. No. 9 hitter Brayan Rocchio led off with a single, and Whitlock issued a one-out walk to third baseman José Ramírez before getting an inning-ending double play from designated hitter Chase DeLauter.
After the Red Sox stranded Duran in the bottom of the eighth, Chapman took the mound for the first time since Sept. 13. Boston’s All-Star closer was back in top form after being day-to-day with lat tightness. He struck out the side, Jo Adell, and pinch-hitters Angel Martínez and Angel Genao on 12 pitches.
The Red Sox are 85-73 with four games left to play. Wednesday marked Tracy’s first win since the interim tag was removed on Tuesday.

item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.description: PITTSBURGH (AP) — Matthew Liberatore ended an 11-start winless stretch and Alec Burleson got his major league-best 112th RBI as the St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-1 on Wednesday night. Liberatore (6-14) gave up one run and six hits in 5 2/3 innings with six strikeouts and no walks. His previous win came on July 11 against Atlanta in the left-hander’s last start before the All-Star break. Liberatore had lost eight straight decisions. Burleson singled in the first run in a t
item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Matthew Liberatore ended an 11-start winless stretch and Alec Burleson got his major league-best 112th RBI as the St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-1 on Wednesday night.
Liberatore (6-14) gave up one run and six hits in 5 2/3 innings with six strikeouts and no walks. His previous win came on July 11 against Atlanta in the left-hander’s last start before the All-Star break. Liberatore had lost eight straight decisions.
Burleson singled in the first run in a three-run third that put the Cardinals ahead 3-1. Iván Herrera scored on a wild pitch and Leo Bernal hit an RBI single.
Masyn Winn doubled home a run and scored on JJ Wetherholt’s single in the fourth to stretch the lead to 5-1. Wetherholt had three hits and José Fermín added two.
The Pirates’ five-game winning streak ended. It matched their longest of the season.
Brandon Lowe accounted for the Pirates’ lone run when he led off the second inning with his team-leading 34th homer, his first of two hits. Ryan O’Hearn had two doubles.
Brandon Eisert (3-3) retired just two of the five betters he faced and was charged with three runs in relief of opener Lake Bachar.
St. Louis (77-81) must win its final four games to avoid its first consecutive losing seasons since 1958 and ’59. Pittsburgh (80-78) needs to at least split its last four games to finish with a winning record for the first time since 2018.
Up next
The rubber match of the three game-series is Thursday, with St. Louis RHP Kyle Leahy (10-5, 3.65 ERA) facing 2025 NL Cy Young Award winner Paul Skenes (10-11, 3.91).
___

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Ben Rice hit his 40th and 41st home runs, Ryan McMahon added a grand slam while matching his career high with five RBIs and the New York Yankees beat the Tampa Bay Rays 9-2 on Wednesday night.
Gerrit Cole (10-9) allowed two runs and three hits in 5 2/3 innings and a season-high 105 pitches with eight strikeouts and three walks. The 2023 AL Cy Young Award winner had a 3.61 ERA and 131 strikeouts over 22 starts and 127 innings following his return in May from Tommy John surgery.
A day after Tampa Bay clinched the AL East title, Rice hit the first pitch of the first inning from Mason Englert (0-4) into the right-field second deck for his fourth career leadoff homer and second this season.
Rice added a solo drive in the fourth for his fifth career multihomer game and finished with three hits. He is tied for the AL home run lead with Baltimore's Pete Alonso, the Rays' Junior Caminero and Houston's Yordan Alvarez.
George Lombard Jr. also homered for the Yankees and Cedric Mullins went deep for the Rays.
New York is assured of hosting a best-of-three AL Wild Card Series starting Tuesday, likely against Boston. The winner will face the Rays in a best-of-five Division Series.
McMahon had an RBI single in the second and boosted the lead to 7-0 in the third with his third career slam.
Englert, brought up to allow Rays starters extra rest ahead of the playoffs, allowed eight runs and nine hits in 4 2/3 innings.
Rays manager Kevin Cash said left-hander Shane McClanahan won't recover in time for the Division Series but left-hander Garrett Cleavinger and right-hander Tyler Wells are possibilities. All three have forearm tightness.
Up next
Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.94 ERA) and Rays RHP Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.56) start Thursday night's series finale.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
The Associated Press

item.title: [roundtable.io] Boston Red Sox' Jarren Duran Joins Exclusive List in Franchise History
item.dc:creator: Zach Coe

BOSTON -- The Boston Red Sox beat the Cleveland Guardians 1-0 on Wednesday night to improve to 85-73 and set up a rubber match on Thursday night. It was supposed to be a night off for struggling outfielder Jarren Duran; however, after center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela exited the game in the third inning with a right hamstring injury, the 30-year-old Duran was thrust into acti
item.content:encoded:
The 30-year-old outfielder stole his 20th base of the season on Wednesday night, joining an exclusive club in team history.
BOSTON -- The Boston Red Sox beat the Cleveland Guardians 1-0 on Wednesday night to improve to 85-73 and set up a rubber match on Thursday night. It was supposed to be a night off for struggling outfielder Jarren Duran; however, after center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela exited the game in the third inning with a right hamstring injury, the 30-year-old Duran was thrust into action, joining an exclusive list in the franchise's 125-year history in the process.
Duran's first at-bat in the third inning ended in disappointment as he struck out with the bases loaded to end the scoring chance for Boston. However, the 30-year-old turned in a strong performance in relief of the injured Rafaela, leading off the bottom of the sixth inning with a single, later coming around to score the game's lone run on a single off the bat of second baseman Andruw Monasterio.
Duran again reached base leading off the eighth inning with a sharply hit line drive to right field. With Boston leading 1-0, the speedster did everything he could to get the team in a position to add on. With third baseman Caleb Durbin at the plate, Duran took off for second base, diving in safely for his 20th stolen base of the year, securing the second 20-home-run, 20-steal season of his career.
Duran became just the third player in Red Sox history to post multiple 20/20 seasons, joining 2018 Most Valuable Player Mookie Betts, who did so three times during his six-year tenure in Boston, and Jackie Jensen, who accomplished the feat twice.
Reaching 20 home runs and 20 steals is an impressive accomplishment for Duran in an otherwise unimpressive season. The 30-year-old has been one of baseball's most disappointing players in 2026, hitting just .207/.265/.364/.629 in 147 games. The 30-year-old ranks in the bottom five among 133 qualified hitters in batting average (129th), on-base percentage (133rd), and OPS (131st).
Despite those struggles, Duran has still found a way to provide some value to the team in both the power and speed departments.
In other Red Sox news
Manager Chad Tracy told reporters, including Tim Healey of the Boston Globe, that Rafaela will undergo an MRI on his right hamstring. Rafaela described the injury as "cramping" that he felt on a swing, rather than when he ran to first base on his second-inning single.
As reported by MassLive.com's Chris Cotillo, 2025 Cy Young Award runner-up Garrett Crochet is scheduled to throw another live bullpen session this weekend as he tries to return from left shoulder inflammation and join the Red Sox in a bullpen role for the postseason. Crochet will not make a regular-season appearance before potentially joining the active roster for the Wild Card round.
With a nor'easter expected to hit New England beginning Friday night, Major League Baseball has moved the Red Sox regular-season finale to Friday afternoon as part of a day-night doubleheader, starting at 1:05 p.m. ET. The league also moved up the start time for Friday's regularly scheduled game from 7:10 p.m. ET to 6:05 p.m. ET. As of now, no changes have been made to Saturday's game.
Up next for the Sox
The Red Sox will look to win the series from the Guardians in Thursday night's rubber match at Fenway Park. Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) will make his final regular-season start for Boston, while Cleveland has not yet named its starter. First pitch is set for 6:45 p.m. ET.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Sonny Gray proves doubters wrong with strong first season starting for the Red Sox in big-market Boston - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Alex Speier
item.description: When the Red Sox landed Sonny Gray in a deal with the Cardinals last November, a question hovered: Could the righthander handle life in a fishbowl? Gray’s first 13 big league seasons had spanned the country, starting on the West Coast (Athletics, 2013-17), crossing over to the East Coast (Yankees, 2017-18), then settling into the Midwest (Reds, 2019-21; Twins, 2022-23; Cardinals, 2024-25). item.content:encoded:
When the Red Sox landed Sonny Gray in a deal with the Cardinals last November, a question hovered: Could the righthander handle life in a fishbowl?
Gray’s first 13 big league seasons had spanned the country, starting on the West Coast (Athletics, 2013-17), crossing over to the East Coast (Yankees, 2017-18), then settling into the Midwest (Reds, 2019-21; Twins, 2022-23; Cardinals, 2024-25). Across teams, he’d mostly been good or great, achieving All-Star recognition in Oakland, Cincinnati, and Minnesota, while notching two 200-strikeout seasons in St. Louis.
There was only one place where he didn’t live up to expectations: New York. As a result, some in the baseball industry concluded Gray was best suited for smaller markets.
Gray, who had the right to veto a trade anywhere he didn’t want to pitch, was aware of the suggestion. Perhaps for that reason, he needed little prodding to approve the trade to the Sox in hopes of laying waste to the suggestion.
“People doubted me just because of my size [entering pro ball]. Stupid, right? So maybe that is something that motivates me: people that talk [expletive] for no reason, just proving them wrong,” said Gray. “Maybe [proving people wrong] does have a little bit of extra motivation inside of me.
“When I left New York in 2018, I told myself that I’m going to go back to a big market at some point in my career. Especially after learning what I learned and having the experiences that I had [in New York], I knew I could [succeed] anywhere after that. So I always told myself that I was going to [pitch again in a large market].”
In the Sox’ 1-0 win Wednesday night over the Guardians, Gray concluded a regular season that served as a compelling testament to his ability to excel in one of the most-scrutinized baseball environments.
With six shutout innings, he finished the year at 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA, setting new career bests in wins and ERA while excelling as a low-velocity, pitch-to-contact artist. He allowed one or no runs in 14 starts.
On and off the mound, the 36-year-old found comfort in Boston, performing at an elite level and comfortable with the intimacy of Fenway and the area.
“I’ve really enjoyed the city. I’ll call it more of like a town, because that’s more what it feels like to me,” said Gray. “[But] I would say this is a pretty big [market]. I’ve enjoyed it. You never know what to expect, but I think the people have been great. I think Fenway is awesome. It’s a very special place.”
Through his comfort, Gray’s success seemingly answered any lingering questions about whether his comfort was tethered to his environment.
“His time in New York was tough and he knows that. I’m sure he wanted to go back and be like, ‘It wasn’t about the market,’ ” said Guardians manager Steven Vogt, who as a former Athletics teammate was behind the plate for the most games and innings thrown by Gray of any catcher in the pitcher’s career, and still considers him a close friend. “Every athlete’s wired differently. But I think for Sonny, getting another opportunity to pitch in a market like this, I think was important to him, and I’m glad that he got to do it.”
Now, Gray will have the opportunity to prove himself as a Red Sox in a different context: the postseason. History suggests he doesn’t fear the stage.
In 2013, as a 23-year-old rookie with just 10 big league starts on his résumé, Gray got the Game 2 starting assignment from the Athletics in the AL Division Series against Tigers ace of aces Justin Verlander, who at that point had six All-Star appearances along with Rookie of the Year, Cy Young, and MVP hardware.
Gray didn’t blink, engaging in an epic pitcher’s duel. Verlander logged seven shutout innings, while Gray posted eight zeros — both pitchers receiving no-decisions in an eventual 1-0 Athletics walkoff win.
“That was one of the greatest games I’ve ever been a part of,” said a beaming Vogt. “You’ve got Justin Verlander, who’d already cemented his path to Cooperstown. Sonny Gray’s throwing his first postseason game in his first season, and going into it, his demeanor, he just was not worried. He was not. He just wanted to go out and pitch.
“That’s the thing about Sonny. He’s one of the fiercest competitors I’ve ever been around. He’s calm, cool, and collected when he’s on the mound, but he’s a killer when he’s on the mound. … They just kept throwing knockouts back and forth.
“It’s his preparation. It’s who he is. He’s always been confident. He’s always been quiet. He’s always just kind of been ready for the moment. There’s no moment too big for him because he’s ready for anything. So I don’t think any of us were shocked that night. It was just more of, we got to watch that.”
Across six career postseason starts, the most recent coming in 2023 with the Twins, Gray is 1-3 with a 3.26 ERA. His teams have won three of his six outings. He is lined up to start for the Sox in next week’s Wild Card Series, likely in New York against the Yankees — affording him one more opportunity to dispel a narrative about his career.
How might that play out?
“If he was on my team,” said Vogt, “there’s no one else I’d rather pitch in a big game.”
Alex Speier can be reached at alex.speier@globe.com. Follow him @alexspeier.

item.content:encoded:
Jarren Duran went 2-for-3 with a stolen base and a run scored off the bench on Wednesday against the Guardians.

Only in this game because Ceddanne Rafaela had to leave early with hamstring tightness, Duran was the spark plug that the Red Sox needed. He helped break a 0-0 tie with a lead-off single in the sixth, advanced to second on a groundout, then came around to score on a single by Andruw Monasterio. That lone run held up as the only scored in this game and Duran stole a base later on as well to give him 20 on the season. That plus his 20 home runs, .207 batting average, and .629 OPS give Duran one of the most disappointing 20-20 seasons of all time.

item.title: [bignewsnetwork.com] Sonny Gray, Red Sox shut out Guardians, who remain 1 up on White Sox
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: Sonny Gray, Red Sox shut out Guardians, who remain 1 up on White Sox (Photo credit: Gregory Fisher) Andruw Monasterio's sixth-inning RBI single and Sonny Gray's six shutout innings propelled the Boston Red Sox to a 1-0 win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night. item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray, Red Sox shut out Guardians, who remain 1 up on White Sox
(Photo credit: Gregory Fisher)
Andruw Monasterio's sixth-inning RBI single and Sonny Gray's six shutout innings propelled the Boston Red Sox to a 1-0 win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night.
The Red Sox (85-73) managed the lone run on 12 hits, all singles. They went 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position and left eight men on base through five innings before Monasterio's run-scoring, two-out knock off Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) broke the deadlock.
In the sixth, Jarren Duran (2-for-3) lined a leadoff single to left and moved to second on a groundout. He scored from second base on Monasterio's knock, sliding ahead of left fielder Steven Kwan's relay throw and catcher Patrick Bailey's tag.
Gray (18-5) struck out three while allowing four hits and one walk to increase his American League-leading win total. Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman each threw a scoreless inning to finish off Boston's 17th shutout victory of the season.
Chapman struck out the side in the ninth to log his 35th save as Boston snapped a three-game losing streak.
Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela returned from a 17-game injury absence caused by a right quad strain to record all three outs in the first, including a spectacular diving catch on Kwan, the leadoff hitter who still went 2-for-4 for Cleveland (82-76).
Griffin worked six frames, striking out seven and allowing one run on 10 hits and no walks.
The Guardians remained one game up on the White Sox (81-77) in the American League Central after Chicago lost 5-4 at Kansas City on Wednesday.
Rafaela hit a leadoff single in the second inning but appeared to be in pain after reaching first. He stayed in the game to run the bases and initially took his defensive position before Duran replaced him. The Red Sox announced that Rafaela was dealing with right hamstring tightness.
Rafaela's defense helped Gray retire the first six men he faced. Bailey recorded Cleveland's first hit with a leadoff single in the third, but a 6-3 double play ended the inning without any damage. Gray fanned a pair of Guardians to strand two to end the fourth.
After the lone run scored and Gray exited, Guerrero struck out three in the seventh after a leadoff walk. Whitlock worked around Brayan Rocchio's leadoff single and Jose Ramirez's one-out walk in the eighth, inducing an inning-ending double-play grounder from Chase DeLauter.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [chicagotribune.com] Column: Alex Bregman’s return and a nor’easter could bring dramatic pause to the Chicago Cubs’ final weekend
item.dc:creator: Paul Sullivan
item.description: It was probably asking too much to expect that Alex Bregman would want to wait until this weekend to return after multiple facial fractures in his left cheek. Bregman was already showing impatience on Wednesday and told reporters he was hoping to get an at-bat in the night game against the Miami Marlins in the potential postseason clincher at Wrigley Field. Craig Counsell heard about Bregman’s request later and paused for a moment when asked if it was a realistic possibility. “Um, no, he’s not g
item.content:encoded:
It was probably asking too much to expect that Alex Bregman would want to wait until this weekend to return after multiple facial fractures in his left cheek.
Bregman was already showing impatience on Wednesday and told reporters he was hoping to get an at-bat in the night game against the Miami Marlins in the potential postseason clincher at Wrigley Field.
Craig Counsell heard about Bregman’s request later and paused for a moment when asked if it was a realistic possibility.
“Um, no, he’s not going to get an at-bat,” the manager said. “He’s not.”
That’s Counsell, always spoiling the media narrative with his insatiable appetite for doing what’s best for the team, ignoring the potential of a drama-filled moment.
“Well, I thought about it last night,” he continued. “We were laughing, (Bregman) got geared up late in the game because he was so fired up. He was like, ‘I was unsure if you were going to yell at me …’
“No, he’s doing well, but we’ve got to take some steps here. I’m excited about how he feels, and he’s excited. But he still needs to feel some things. He hasn’t run around yet, and he’s got to do that. He’s got to know what it feels like.”
Bregman spoke to the media Wednesday for the first time since taking a foul ball off his left cheek in Sunday’s win in Cincinnati. He avoided surgery but suffered multiple facial fractures and had to be driven back to Chicago instead of flying. There were small lacerations visible under his left eye on Wednesday, and his eye was still blackened, making it look like he’d spent a couple rounds with Mike Tyson.
The initial jolt of pain was excruciating, Bregman admitted.
“I kind of just looked down and felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face,” he said. “The pain has been fine. I guess I fractured something right by the nerve in my face, so the whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb. As soon as the swelling goes down, I’m sure I’ll feel the breaks a little bit more.
“It started last night because the swelling is going down, and I felt that this morning when I woke up. All in all, I’m super lucky it hit where it hit, and a lot of gratitude because a few centimeters higher and it could’ve been detrimental.”
Bregman said he never thought about a “worst-case” scenario when it happened, and just hoped nothing was broken. Now he considered himself to be “in a good spot,” making him anxious to return.
“We’ve got really good news the last two days,” he said. “So overall I’ve been very lucky, and I’m very thankful to all the doctors and everybody that helped out.”
Bregman said he’s feeling a little better every day. Wednesday was what he described as a “normal” work day — hitting off the Trajekt machine — after spending Tuesday tracking off the machine, which replicates velocities and spin rates of pitchers.
He said he planned to test out some different batting helmets that would protect his left cheek, and didn’t feel it would take long to adjust to one. He’s had no issues seeing, and there was no damage to his eyesight, which allowed him to use the Trajekt machine to track pitches.
“I see it great,” he said.
Bregman hoped to take grounders in a day or two, though it seems likely he would return in a designated hitter role, at least initially, instead of going straight back to third base.
Bregman had played in 153 of the Cubs’ 156 games before missing Tuesday’s loss to the Marlins, which denied the Cubs the clincher. Kevin Gausman faced the Marlins on Wednesday with the Cubs in a three-way tie with the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres in the National League wild-card race, and a magic number of one to get in.
Even before the injury, Bregman hated being out of the Cubs’ lineup.
After a slow first half in which he repeatedly said his numbers would be there by the end of the season, he rebounded to his normal All-Star level, as he predicted. On Wednesday, Bregman ranked second in major-league RBI in the second half with 48, trailing only Pete Crow-Armstrong’s 54. He was also fifth in OPS (.978) since the break, and third in WAR (3.4), while playing Gold Glove Award-caliber defense.
“Super tough,” he said of sitting. “Yesterday was brutal. I wanted to play.”
Asked about the biggest hurdle of his recovery, Bregman said he wasn’t sure, then mentioned the feeling of constant movement in his upper face.
“There’s a lot of fluid in my face over there,” he said of his left side. “So if I move, the fluid moves. So if I’m bouncing up and down, my face feels like it’s bouncing up and down.”
Counsell said it was “not a surprise” that Bregman was impatient about returning, but noted the severity of the injury forced them to take it slow.
“We’ve got to understand what he has, and you’ve got to be careful,” Counsell said. “We’ve got to go through the proper channels here and (take) the proper steps.”
Bregman’s first game back could be Friday in Boston, where he played in 2025 before exercising an opt-out clause in his contract and signing a five-year, $175 million deal with the Cubs. Due to the possibility of a nor’easter, the Cubs will now play a doubleheader against the Red Sox on Friday at Fenway Park, avoiding a potential cancellation on Sunday.
It would be easy for the Cubs to sideline Bregman until the postseason out of an abundance of caution, giving him extra time to heal. No one would bat an eye, except perhaps for Bregman.
President Jed Hoyer said Tuesday, “getting hit again is a concern, but most of the significant bad things have been avoided.”
Why risk it when he’s such an important part of the lineup?
That’s a question the Cubs might have to ask themselves as he tries to get back as quickly as possible. The playoffs are what’s important now, and it’s hard to imagine the Cubs being the Cubs without Bregman’s presence in the lineup.
But for now they’re deferring to Bregman, which creates the possibility of a dramatic return to Fenway Park with a nor’easter on the way and the Cubs fighting for home-field advantage in the wild-card round. Maybe Theo Epstein will even make an appearance.
John Updike couldn’t come up with a more appropriate way to bid the Cubs’ regular season adieu.

item.title: [cubbiescrib.com] Andy Green's former Cubs boss is one of the biggest losers in his sudden change of heart
item.dc:creator: Jake Misener

item.content:encoded:
Since being tapped as interim manager, Andy Green remained adamant he did not want the job long-term. Well, something changed and, now, the former Chicago Cubs bench coach is the man in Queens after signing a three-year extension that was announced on Tuesday.
It's been the better part of a decade since Green last managed. Prior to serving as Cubs bench coach, he was the skipper of the San Diego Padres from 2016-2019. After being fired in Sept. 2019, he came to Chicago as the right-hand man for first-time manager David Ross, who took over following the departure of Joe Maddon.
Baseball often has a funny way of bringing things full circle and with the interim tag coming off Green, Ross is among those who directly felt the impact of the move. The beloved former big-league backstop hasn't coached or managed since the Cubs dumped him for Craig Counsell prior to the 2024 campaign, but remains a logical candidate for any vacancy that opens.
Unfortunately for him, that list of potential opportunities just shrank by one as Green, who has thrived both in the clubhouse and with the media this year since stepping in for the fired Carlos Mendoza, takes another bite as an MLB manager.
David Ross could still see opportunities to get a new managerial gig
Crossing the Mets' job off the list, let's take a spin around the league to see which other managers could be on the outs. Really, it boils down to three (maybe four) gigs after Craig Breslow and Chad Tracy got some long-term certainty in Boston: Houston, Seattle, Arizona and, potentially, Philadelphia.
It feels like a foregone conclusion that the Astros, Mariners and Diamondbacks will be looking for new managers at season's end. Joe Espada, Dan Wilson and Torey Lovullo are all aware of that fact and, given the fact that none of those teams seem particularly likely to embark on immediate teardowns, they could seek a manager with some experience (enter Ross).
He'll face some stiff competition. The field of candidates include a pair of Hall of Famers in Albert Pujols and Carlos Beltran and a former World Series champion in the dugout in Alex Cora. That doesn't even take into account the dark horse candidates that always pop into these conversations.
That all being said, this partnership between Green and the Mets seems like a win-win for everyone involved... unless you're David Ross.

Bregman spoke to reporters Wednesday prior to the Cubs’ game against the Miami Marlins, and despite his rough appearance, he says he’s feeling very fortunate that the injury wasn’t worse. “(I was) super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn’t a few centimeters higher,” he said. Bregman was standing near the o
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is still sporting a heck of a shiner after being struck by a foul ball, but could he be back in the lineup this weekend?
Bregman spoke to reporters Wednesday prior to the Cubs’ game against the Miami Marlins, and despite his rough appearance, he says he’s feeling very fortunate that the injury wasn’t worse.
“(I was) super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn’t a few centimeters higher,” he said.
Bregman was standing near the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds when Michael Busch hit a foul ball with a check swing. The ball bounced once off the turf and hit Bregman just below his left eye.
According to the Cubs, Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures, but the team has not put him on the injured list with less than a week to go in the regular season, and he’s aiming to get back in the lineup in enough time to be ready for the playoffs he hopes the Cubs are competing in.
“Yeah. I hope so,” Bregman said when asked if he would play in this weekend’s series against the Boston Red Sox.
Manager Craig Counsell didn’t commit to trying to get Bregman back on the field in the coming days, but said he was happy with his progress so far.
Local
“He’s still got significant swelling in his face and his eye that needs to improve,” he said. “But all things considered, he’s in a good place.”
Despite Counsell’s apprehension, Bregman said he would have tried to get in the lineup for Wednesday night’s game if he could have.
“I’m going to try to get in there tonight,” he said.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox have secured a postseason berth. Now they need their offense to look ready for October. Boston enters Wednesday’s game against the Cleveland Guardians on a three-game losing streak. The Red Sox have scored two runs or fewer in each of those losses, putting more attention on the lineup Chad Tracy will send out against Cleveland left-hander Foster Griffin.
Jahmai Jones is batting third again, between Nick Sogard and Wilyer Abreu. Roman Anthony leads off, while Adley Rutschman bats fifth after collecting three hits, including two doubles, in Tuesday’s 3-2 loss.
The Red Sox announced Wednesday’s lineup ahead of the 7:10 p.m. ET game at Fenway Park.
Red Sox Lineup Vs. Guardians On Wednesday
- Roman Anthony, LF
- Nick Sogard, 1B
- Jahmai Jones, DH
- Wilyer Abreu, RF
- Adley Rutschman, C
- Ceddanne Rafaela, CF
- Caleb Durbin, 3B
- Trevor Story, SS
- Andruw Monasterio, 2B
Sonny Gray will start for Boston against Griffin.
Tonight's crew. pic.twitter.com/80BRyMRZI7
— Red Sox (@RedSox) September 23, 2026
Jones’ place in the order is worth watching. Batting him third puts a right-handed hitter between Sogard and Abreu against a left-handed starter. It also gives Jones another opportunity to strengthen his case for a significant postseason role.
Offense Needs To Step Up
Rutschman gave Boston one of its few bright spots Tuesday, but the Red Sox could not build enough offense around him. Mickey Gasper’s pinch-hit homer tied the game in the eighth inning before Cleveland pulled out the win. Boston has dropped five of its last seven games.
Gray enters Wednesday with a 17-5 record and a 2.82 ERA. A strong outing from him would help stop the skid, but the Red Sox also need to see more from a lineup that has gone quiet at an uncomfortable time.
Boston is postseason-bound. Wednesday offers a chance to start playing like it.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Ceddanne Rafaela leaves first Red Sox game back from injured list (leg)
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: Ceddanne Rafaela’s first game back from the 10-day injured list (right quad strain) lasted all of two innings before the Red Sox removed him for seemingly precautionary reasons. item.content:encoded:
Ceddanne Rafaela’s first game back from the 10-day injured list (right quad strain) lasted all of two innings before the Red Sox removed him for seemingly precautionary reasons.
Boston’s Gold Glove center fielder caught all three outs in the top of the first, even laying out for a diving catch of Cleveland Guardians’ Steven Kwan’s leadoff line drive.
But when Rafaela singled to lead off the bottom of the second, he grimaced as he ran and seemed to pull up lame on first base. He leaned over briefly as he stood on the bag, prompting a visit from manager Chad Tracy and a team trainer. After a few minutes’ discussion and some test running down the first base line, they allowed Rafaela to remain in the game.
Rafaela appeared to run normally as he advanced to second when Caleb Durbin reached first on a fielding error by third baseman José Ramírez, and initially remained on the field after the Red Sox failed to score in the bottom of the second. But Jarren Duran replaced him in center before the top of the third began.
“Just saw him continuing to flex it,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy told ESPN’s Buster Olney moments later on the game broadcast. “That’s all. He seemed to have felt some cramping in the back there. When he went back out there, he kept flexing it, so we said, let’s go ahead and make the change.”
Red Sox media relations announced Rafaela left the game with “right hamstring tightness” two innings later.
The Red Sox already planned to monitor Rafaela’s workload in Wednesday’s game, as the end of the Triple-A season on Sunday meant he returned without playing in single a rehab game.
“You guys know, every ball that gets hit up in the air in his direction, he thinks he can catch it,” Tracy said pregame. “So if you have a very normal, easy game flow, I think he’d be just fine. If you have a game flow where he tracks down seven balls in the gap and hits two doubles, you might say that’s enough.
“We’ll be very reactive to what the game is requiring of him and do our best to make sure we keep him in a good spot.”
Rafaela’s departure had consequences for the Red Sox almost immediately. They loaded the bases in the bottom of the third on back-to-back singles by Roman Anthony and Nick Sogard, and a two-out single by Adley Rutschman. Duran, batting in Rafaela’s No. 6 spot in the order, struck out swinging to end the inning.

item.content:encoded:
Ceddanne Rafaela was removed from Wednesday’s game against the Guardians with right hamstring tightness.

Rafaela was lifted from the contest shortly after he pulled up awkwardly and doubled over in discomfort following a second-inning single to left field. He managed to stay in the game initially, but was removed for a defensive replacement in the next inning. The 26-year-old center fielder was playing in his first game back after missing two weeks with a quad strain. The hope for the Red Sox is that his early departure was out of an abundance of caution. There should be an additional update on his status following the contest.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox have a better playoff call-up option than Braiden Ward waiting in Fort Myers
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: Barring an unforeseen collapse or miracle, the Boston Red Sox will be heading to New York for the Wild Card series for the second consecutive season. After scoring just six runs in their three-game series against the Yankees last year — including a shutout in the decisive Game 3 — it figures that the offense will be the primary topic of conversation prior to the 2026 iteration of this epic playoff rivalry. item.content:encoded:
Barring an unforeseen collapse or miracle, the Boston Red Sox will be heading to New York for the Wild Card series for the second consecutive season. After scoring just six runs in their three-game series against the Yankees last year — including a shutout in the decisive Game 3 — it figures that the offense will be the primary topic of conversation prior to the 2026 iteration of this epic playoff rivalry.
That's especially true right now, since the Red Sox have apparently completely lost their ability to hit in clutch situations over the past month. For reference, in nine of their first 15 games of September, they went hitless or managed just one hit with runners in scoring position.
That has a lot of people wondering: Is it time to do something drastic to shake up the run-production unit? Hence, the idea of calling up speed demon Braiden Ward has started to gain some traction recently, since he's managed a whopping 61 steals in 109 games in Worcester this year.
The problem, of course, is that the Red Sox need someone who can deliver hits with runners in scoring position, rather than just someone who can get in scoring position. And if a call-up is in the cards, it's clear that Romy Gonzalez is most deserving. He and Ward are both part of a "stay ready" squad the Red Sox have sent to Fort Myers in the event of a playoff call-up.
Romy Gonzalez has earned another stint with Red Sox following torrid stretch in Worcester
Gonzalez didn't have the easiest time in Boston earlier this year, posting a 59 wRC+ over 19 games after being activated off the 60-day injured list. Since being sent down to Triple-A to work on his game in early August, however, he was a total menace at the plate in the final weeks of the WooSox season: he hit .355/.410/.538 with 11 extra-base hits in just 93 at-bats.
That's the kind of run-producing bat the big-league club needs at the moment. There is merit in giving Ward a bench role in the playoffs — his speed and defense would be huge assets late in games — but nothing he provides would be as valuable as having Gonzalez's career 131 wRC+ against southpaws available at a moment's notice.
Another consideration? Ward, who has never played in the majors, isn't currently on the 40-man roster and would need to be added ahead of a playoff series, displacing someone else. That would probably be as simple as stashing Curtis Mead on the 60-day IL, but it would also begin Ward's service time clock just ahead of the impending lockout.
With all due respect to Ward, the Red Sox already made their call on him at the trade deadline, when they acquired a player with a very similar profile in Eli White. His injury may have seemingly opened the door for a call-up, but with runs at a premium in October, the wisest course of action is to go with the bat-first player with extensive MLB action under his belt.

item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO (AP) — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is thankful he’s not a little shorter.
Sporting a discolored left eye after being struck by a foul ball in the on-deck circle Sunday, the three-time All-Star said it could’ve been worse.
“Super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn’t a few centimeters higher,” he said before Wednesday night’s game against Miami.
The ball, off the bat of teammate Michael Busch in Cincinnati, caused several facial fractures.
With the postseason approaching, the Cubs are glad the injury won’t require a stint on the injured list.
Bregman said he’ll likely start shagging ground balls in a day or so and will be trying out new styles of helmets to protect the eye.
“The whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb,” he said.
The Cubs can clinch an NL wild-card berth with a win Wednesday night or an Arizona loss.
“He’s still got significant swelling in his face and his eye that needs to improve,” Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Tuesday. “But all things considered, he’s in a good place.”
Bregman was on deck in the fourth inning of a 9-1 win at Cincinnati when he was hit on the left side of his face by Busch’s check-swing foul. Bregman immediately jogged toward the Cubs’ dugout and covered his face before going back to the clubhouse with an athletic trainer.
“When everything was going down on Sunday afternoon, I think that we all thought the worst case might be a possibility,” president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer said Tuesday. “And all the news since then has been really good. He’s had a lot of different doctor’s appointments, and they’ve been positive. And I think we have to take it one step at a time.”
Bregman is batting .262 with 26 homers and 89 RBIs in 153 games during his first season with Chicago. He signed a $175 million, five-year contract with the Cubs in free agency.
The 32-year-old Bregman got off to a rough start in his new home, hitting just .229 with two homers in his first 20 games. But he has been one of Chicago’s most productive players since the All-Star break, batting .305 with 17 homers and 48 RBIs in his last 57 games.
Bregman also has excelled in the postseason in the past. He won two World Series championships with the Houston Astros. He appeared in at least two postseason games in each of the previous nine years.
___

item.title: [foxnews.com] Sonny Gray and the Boston Red Sox host Cleveland Guardians in a potential MLB playoffs preview
item.dc:creator: David Troy
item.description: The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team. Tonight, I'm going for a game that we could potentially see in the playoffs as the Guardians take on the Red Sox. The Guardians are currently the owners of the top spot in the
item.content:encoded:
The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team.
Tonight, I'm going for a game that we could potentially see in the playoffs as the Guardians take on the Red Sox.
The Guardians are currently the owners of the top spot in the American League Central. As seems to be the case for Cleveland every season, they saved their best baseball for the end of the season. They've won six straight games, but they are only one game ahead of the White Sox, who have also won three straight games. The good news for both of them is that, as long as they both are winning games, they can both make the postseason. The magic number for the Guardians to make the playoffs is down to one.
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
Giving them a great chance today is the arm they acquired at the trade deadline, Foster Griffin. For the season, Griffin is 15-5 with a 3.67 ERA and a 1.19 WHIP. Griffin, overall, has been a nice addition to the team. He has two starts that were a little bit of a disaster, going four innings against the Mets and allowing five earned in his debut with the Guardians.
The Baltimore Orioles also knocked him around for eight runs in 2.1 innings. His other six starts saw him going for 22 innings and allow just 11 runs. He has never faced the Red Sox, so he could have them off balance the first time through the lineup.
The Boston Red Sox are one of those teams that are likely brimming with confidence. After a disaster of a start to their season, they pivoted and became one of the hottest teams in baseball right before the All-Star Break. They continue to be a streaky team, but the majority of their streaks have seen them winning games instead of losing them. They are still just an average team at Fenway with a 38-38 record for the season. It is almost hard to believe given how good they've been, but getting to .500 is impressive because of how bad they were early in the year.
The Red Sox are sending the one guy who was dominant at home all year, Sonny Gray. For the season, Sonny Gray is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA and a 1.16 WHIP. He should be in the running for the Cy Young Award, even though he won't win over Cam Schlittler. He's been solid in September, going 19.1 innings and allowing a total of six earned runs. He faced the Guardians earlier this season and allowed just one earned run over six innings in a 9-1 win for the Red Sox.
It wasn't just that one game against the Guardians that Gray has excelled in. He has been great against them for years, holding hitters to a .208 batting average over 130 at-bats. Although the Red Sox don't really "need" this game to solidify their Wild Card spot, they still should look to win. Gray has been dominant for them, and they've been very successful in his outings this year. I'm backing the Red Sox here and I also think they probably cover the -1.5 run line. I also would be surprised to see this game go under 6.5 runs. I'll play all three bets.

item.content:encoded:
El final de la temporada de la Liga Americana ( MLB ) está a la vuelta de la esquina, y a la mayoría de los equipos les quedan unas cinco jornadas, contando la de hoy. Todavía hay algunos partidos emocionantes hoy y este fin de semana. Ayer nos fue 1-1: perdimos con los Angels y ganamos en el partido entre los Rays y los Yankees. Supongo que debería saber que no hay que apostar por un equipo que lleva 100 derrotas.
Esta noche voy a ver un partido que quizá podamos volver a ver en los playoffs: los Guardians se enfrentan a los Red Sox.
Los Guardians ocupan ahora mismo el primer puesto de la División Central de la Liga Americana. Como suele pasar con Cleveland cada temporada, han reservado su mejor juego para el final de la temporada. Han ganado seis partidos seguidos, pero solo llevan un partido de ventaja sobre los White Sox, que también llevan tres victorias seguidas. La buena noticia para ambos es que, mientras sigan ganando partidos, los dos pueden clasificarse para la postemporada. El número mágico para que los Guardians se clasifiquen para los playoffs se ha reducido a uno.
Esta página puede contener enlaces de afiliados a socios de apuestas deportivas legales. Si te registras o realizas una apuesta, FOX News podría recibir una compensación. Este contenido lo ha creado un equipo que trabaja de forma independiente de la redacción de FOX News.
Hoy tienen una gran oportunidad gracias al lanzador que ficharon en el cierre del mercado de traspasos: Foster Griffin. En lo que va de temporada, Griffin lleva un balance de 15-5, con una ERA de 3,67 y un WHIP de 1,19. En general, Griffin ha sido una buena incorporación para el equipo. Ha tenido dos salidas que fueron un poco desastrosas: aguantó cuatro entradas contra los Mets y encajó cinco carreras limpias en su debut con los Guardians.
Los Orioles de Baltimore también le endosaron ocho carreras en 2,1 entradas. En sus otras seis salidas como titular, lanzó 22 entradas y solo encajó 11 carreras. Nunca se ha enfrentado a los Red Sox, así que podría desconcertarlos en la primera vuelta por el orden de bateo.
Los Boston Red Sox son uno de esos equipos que seguramente están rebosantes de confianza. Tras un comienzo de temporada desastroso, dieron un giro y se convirtieron en uno de los equipos más en racha del béisbol justo antes del parón del All-Star. Siguen siendo un equipo con altibajos, pero en la mayoría de sus rachas han ganado partidos en lugar de perderlos. Siguen siendo solo un equipo normalito en Fenway, con un balance de 38-38 en lo que va de temporada. Cuesta casi creerlo, teniendo en cuenta lo bien que lo han hecho, pero llegar al 50 % es impresionante si tenemos en cuenta lo mal que lo hicieron a principios de año.
Los Red Sox van a sacar al único que ha estado imparable en casa todo el año: Sonny Gray. En lo que va de temporada, Sonny Gray lleva un balance de 17-5, con una ERA de 2,82 y un WHIP de 1,16. Debería estar en la pugna por el Premio Cy Young, aunque no va a ganarle a Cam Schlittler. Ha estado muy sólido en septiembre, lanzando 19,1 entradas y cediendo un total de seis carreras limpias. Se enfrentó a los Guardians a principios de temporada y solo cedió una carrera limpia en seis entradas, en una victoria por 9-1 de los Red Sox.
No ha sido solo en ese partido contra los Guardians donde Gray ha destacado. Lleva años jugando genial contra ellos, manteniendo a los bateadores en un promedio de bateo de 0,208 en más de 130 turnos al bate. Aunque los Red Sox no «necesitan» realmente este partido para afianzar su plaza de comodín, igual deberían intentar ganar. Gray ha estado impresionante para ellos y les ha ido muy bien en sus salidas este año. Apuesto por los Red Sox en este partido y también creo que probablemente cubrirán el hándicap de -1,5 carreras. Además, me sorprendería que el total de carreras de este partido fuera inferior a 6,5. Voy a hacer las tres apuestas.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Garrett Crochet ‘probably not’ going to pitch for Red Sox in regular season
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: If Garrett Crochet returns to the Red Sox pitching staff this year, it will almost certainly be in October. “As far as the regular season, yeah, I think that’s probably not going to happen,” manager Chad Tracy said Wednesday afternoon, hours before the Red Sox and visiting Cleveland Guardians played Game 158 of 162. The left-hander came through his live batting practice session on Tuesday well, but the Red Sox want him to throw another live BP this weekend. “I heard he felt pretty good today, wh
item.content:encoded:
If Garrett Crochet returns to the Red Sox pitching staff this year, it will almost certainly be in October.
“As far as the regular season, yeah, I think that’s probably not going to happen,” manager Chad Tracy said Wednesday afternoon, hours before the Red Sox and visiting Cleveland Guardians played Game 158 of 162.
The left-hander came through his live batting practice session on Tuesday well, but the Red Sox want him to throw another live BP this weekend.
“I heard he felt pretty good today, which is encouraging,” Tracy said of his star southpaw. “All things considered, that was his first real tense live.”
But Crochet’s schedule, like that of the team he so badly wants to rejoin, is in flux due to the nor’easter expected to pummel the Boston area this weekend. The Red Sox and Cubs already moved Sunday’s Game 162 to a split-doubleheader on Friday, but could potentially change the time or location of Saturday’s night’s game.
“More logistics,” Tracy said. “With weather, like, where are we doing that (live BP)?”
Though Tracy said effectively ruling out a regular-season return for Crochet “doesn’t necessarily void him for the Wild Card,” he stressed the complexity of the situation.
“The conversations around that are deep in a lot of ways,” Tracy said. “Like it could change a playoff roster. What is he able to give you? Can he give you two games? Can he give you multiple innings? Can he go back-to-back? All those questions have to be answered, not only for his own health, but for our team and what puts us in the best position.”
“In Garrett’s situation, that we’re talking about the ace of our staff, I think a lot of the conversation is hovering around, is it feasible to do that?” Tracy continued. “And what can he give us? How does it affect the rest of the roster? And what kind of spot are we putting him in? Are we comfortable doing that?
“I think it’s mostly related around our comfort with his health, and then we’ll go from there.”

Every Monday, Tom empties out his notebook over email and covers MLB’s hottest topics, provides in-depth analysis through both text and video breakdowns, looks forward to what’s worth watching during the week and more.
Ronald Acuña Jr. of the Braves may be hitting .259 with career lows in exit velocity and hard-hit rate, but don’t be fooled by the overall stats. If the star outfielder can fight through a left shin contusion he suffered Tuesday night on a foul ball at the plate—he’s currently considered day-to-day—he’ll be a force to be reckoned with in October. Ever since mid-August when Acuña began to knock off the rust from two IL stints, he’s been a dangerous, dynamic hitter.
The tell-tale sign is how Acuña is getting to high fastballs he used to miss.
| Acuna vs. 95+ MPH | No. | BA | SLG | HR | Attack Angle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Through Aug. 22 | 315 | .183 | .268 | 1 | 9° |
| Since | 119 | .393 | .857 | 4 | 7° |
Pitchers were dominating Acuña with velocity over his hands. No more. Acuña has made the adjustment. While his barrel had been working underneath the pitch plane, now he is flattening his attack angle, as you can see here:
Acuña heads my list of hitters who are most likely to cap a disappointing year with a strong finish.
Down Year but Primed for Big October
1. Ronald Acuña Jr., Braves
2. Mookie Betts, Dodgers
3. Will Smith, Dodgers
4. Trevor Story, Red Sox
5. José Ramírez, Guardians
Gerrit Cole, Game 2 Starter?
Yankees righthander Gerrit Cole broke through a late-season slump with an improved outing Friday in Arizona (six innings, two earned runs).
As I said last week here, Cole has been throwing too many strikes in the middle of the plate. His fix: tighten the delivery to be more compact and move almost six inches on the rubber toward the third base side.
A frequent tinkerer, Cole began the season toward the center of the rubber but after the Red Sox pounded him for four runs June 27, he moved to the first base side July 3 and stayed there for 13 starts. But after his poor start Sept. 12 against the Mets, which included a career high of hard hits, he returned to the center.
Here you can see his foot position change on the rubber in his past two starts:
It’s the quickest fix to a command issue. You don’t need to change mechanics, just the lane in which the ball leaves your hand.
How did it work? His command was much better. Look at his fastball heat maps and it’s clear he did a better job of keeping the ball out of the center lane:
Cole Fastball Heat Maps
This start moved Cole closer to getting the ball ahead of Max Fried or Carlos Rodon (or both) in a wild-card series against Boston.
As usual, Cole pounded the zone. He has not issued a walk among 71 batters faced in his past three starts. But still a concern: the swing-and-miss still has not returned to his game. He had only six swings-and-misses against Arizona. His September whiff rate is 17%, down from 22.4% entering the month.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone will have a difficult decision in choosing who starts after Schlittler, a decision that should be based on how Cole, Fried and Rodon are throwing the ball rather than sheer numbers or opponent trends. The Red Sox are slightly better against left-handed pitching (24–15, .746 OPS) than right-handed (60–55, .713 OPS), though the return of Roman Anthony changes that a bit.
📺 TV on TV This Week
Sunday, Sept. 27: Postseason Preview, 8 p.m. ET (MLB Network)
Up to 53 pressure-packed games in 33 days. The best month in all of sports is just about here.
I’ll’ll also be recording a playoff preview show on Monday along with MLB editor Will Laws and staff writer Ryan Phillips. Look out for that on our

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Potential Reunion with Sonny Gray Makes Sense for Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Curt Bishop; Unknown
item.description: Last offseason, the St. Louis Cardinals traded Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Nolan Arenado and Brendan Donovan, stripping their roster of established veteran players. However, that seemed to have lit a spark underneath the young players they have on their roster. Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt have emerged as franchise cornerstones, and though they have cooled off towards the end of the season, there is still a lot to be excited about when concerning the future. The Cardinals also saw Alec Bur
item.content:encoded:
Last offseason, the St. Louis Cardinals traded Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Nolan Arenado and Brendan Donovan, stripping their roster of established veteran players. However, that seemed to have lit a spark underneath the young players they have on their roster.
Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt have emerged as franchise cornerstones, and though they have cooled off towards the end of the season, there is still a lot to be excited about when concerning the future. The Cardinals also saw Alec Burleson emerge as a star.
Though their starting rotation has been their strength, it could use an addition or two in the offseason. Perhaps a reunion with Sonny Gray could make sense.
Why Sonny Gray reunion would make sense
Gray wasn't quite the ace the Cardinals needed him to be in his two years in St. Louis, but he has been that guy for the Boston Red Sox. In 28 starts, the 36-year-old right-hander is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA. Though he is older now, he would make sense for the Cardinals because he will likely cost a little less than he did when St. Louis orginally signed him after the 2023 season.
He's also a proven veteran leader that can guide the young pitching staff, and is somebody that can anchor the rotation and get them one step closer to returning to postseason contention, and if they struggle again, he could be a trade candidate at the deadline.
But now might be the right time for the Cardinals to supplement what they have already built from within. They have a strong core in place, and some proven pieces could be what they need to take the next step forward in 2027.
Gray does have a mutual option with Boston for 2027 and has considered retirement, but the mutual option will likely be declined. And if he doesn't retire, perhaps he'll see what the Cardinals have built and be interested in returning to St. Louis.
He is a voice that a lot of the Cardinals' young players are familiar with. He also seemed to enjoy his time in St. Louis despite the team's struggles, and with Kyle Leahy, Quinn Mathews and Michael McGreevy emerging, St. Louis could have an even stronger starting rotation in 2027, especially since the farm system is now loaded with pitching, including top prospect Liam Doyle.
There is a lot to be excited about, and signing Gray could be the first step to getting St. Louis back into contention.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. item.content:encoded:
BOSTON, MA—The Boston Red Sox today reinstated outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela from the 10-Day Injured List. To make room, Boston optioned infielder/outfielder Nate Eaton.
Rafaela, 26, was placed on the 10-Day Injured List on September 6 (retroactive to September 3) with a right quadriceps strain. The right-handed hitter has batted .282 (151-for-535) with 32 doubles, three triples, 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 67 runs scored, and a .760 OPS in 135 games this season, while making 130 starts in center field. He also earned his first career All-Star selection. Signed by Boston as an international free agent in July 2017, the Curaçao native has batted .258 (441-for-1,708) with 95 doubles, 12 triples, 49 home runs, 213 RBI, and a.709 OPS in 471 career Major League games, all for the Red Sox (2023-26).
Eaton, 29, has played in 23 games this season for Boston, going 7-for-48 with two doubles and one home run while making six starts in left field, six in center field, and three in right field. The right-handed hitter has also played in 84 games for Worcester this year, hitting .253 (79-for-312) with 16 doubles, three triples, nine home runs, 44 RBI, 58 runs scored, and a .748 OPS while making 49 starts in center field, 15 in right field, 12 in left field, and three as the designated hitter. Originally selected by the Kansas City Royals in the 21st round of the 2018 First-Year Player Draft, the Virginia native has hit .219 (63-for-288) in 136 career Major League Games for the Royals (2022-23) and Red Sox (2025-26).
